Eyewitness testimony on Tina Kotek. This also mirrors the pattern in the state gov't agency I worked in. These environments are like Franz Kafka's "The Castle". I was reading Kafka one lunch break day in my cubicle & started laughing. Oh, I work in "The Castle"!! 

These environments are batshit crazy. One year I got sent to "The Basics of Supervision" training. OMG. As supervisors we were to diagnose our employees for mental illnesses. My PSU social worker managers' textbook held up Adolf Hitler as a role model. Book, of course written by a German.

Tina appears to be like those girl bullies in junior high school?

Testimony from Diego Hernandez:
"I’m not voting for Tina Kotek.
I personally know Tina Kotek’s Leadership. I Experienced It.

I’ve been watching Tina Kotek’s governorship and the growing frustration with her leadership, the staff turnover, the controversies, and the struggles to deliver on some of Oregon’s most pressing issues.

And I can’t help but reflect on my own experience.

I served four years in the Oregon House of Representatives under Tina Kotek’s leadership as Speaker. I worked directly with her. I experienced how she treated people who challenged her authority, disagreed with her decisions, or refused to fall in line.

I was bullied, harassed, threatened, and politically targeted by Tina Kotek. I don’t say that lightly. I lived it, documented it, provided evidence and witnesses, and eventually testified publicly about it.

And what I experienced says a lot about the kind of leadership I believe Oregon has been subjected to.

—When Power Becomes a Tool for Control—
I still remember one of my first meetings with Tina when I was newly elected.

There wasn’t much interest in getting to know me, understanding the communities I represented, or discussing the policies I wanted to champion.

Instead, I was told how much money I was expected to raise for the Democratic caucus and how my ability to advance legislation, secure committee assignments, and receive political support would depend on meeting those expectations.

That was my introduction to legislative leadership.

Now, I understand politics. I understand fundraising, negotiating, coalition building, and the difficult compromises that come with governing. I’ve participated in all of it.
But there’s a difference between exercising political leadership and using institutional power to intimidate, punish, and control people.

Over time, I came to experience Tina’s leadership as rooted in fear, coercion, manipulation, and political retaliation.

The message was clear: Support what she wants, or risk losing what matters to you.

And when you represent communities that have historically been excluded from political power, that kind of leverage can be particularly harmful.

—The Day She Threatened My Career—
In 2019, Tina was trying to pass controversial legislation changing Oregon’s public employee retirement system, commonly known as PERS.
I disagreed with the legislation and refused to vote for it.

That decision led to repeated pressure and threats. And during one of her escalating confrontations towards me, Tina told me directly:

“I will make sure to end your career.”
She threatened my legislative priorities, my political future, and bills I had worked hard to advance.

In one of her final attempts to get me to change my vote, she said she was going to kill the legislation to restore access to driver’s licenses for undocumented Oregonians if I voted no.
Think about that for a moment.

A policy affecting thousands of immigrant families, people who needed to drive legally to work, take their children to school, and participate in everyday life, was being used as leverage to force my vote on an entirely unrelated issue.

I wasn’t going to let that happen.

Immediately after that threat, I called Rep. Teresa Alonso Leon, who was working with me on the driver’s license legislation, and told her what Tina was threatening to do.

Teresa was courageous and she told Tina that if she killed our driver’s license bill, Teresa would change her vote on PERS from yes to a no.
With the vote already extremely close, losing another vote completely threatened Tina’s ability to pass the legislation.

That changed the political equation.

The PERS bill barely passed, but only after Democrat changed their vote from no to yes. That legislator had been called into Tina’s office and, from what I witnessed, emerged in tears, visibly distressed by the vote they felt compelled to make.

Our driver’s license legislation survived thanks to Teresa Alonso Leon and eventually became law.
But I never forgot what it took to protect it.
What disturbed me most was how easily the needs of an entire community could become bargaining chips in an effort to control another elected official.

And this was only one example of what I experienced.

—When the System Protects Power—
I eventually filed a formal workplace harassment complaint and provided evidence of Tina’s conduct, including contemporaneous messages, witnesses, and documentation of the threats. Tina worked hard to make sure the investigation never concluded or to come out and see the light of day, dragging far beyond the required time required by statute.

People witnessed parts of what happened. I told colleagues about the threats immediately after they occurred, long before there was any formal investigation.

The independent investigator even concluded that the evidence more closely supported my version of events.

Yet the investigator reasoned that conduct potentially inappropriate in another workplace was different in the Legislature because politics is inherently contentious. Mind you that investigator is under the office controlled by Tina herself. These investigators work like prosecutors for her office.

Essentially, the intimidation I experienced was treated as part of politics. The House Conduct Committee ultimately deadlocked 2–2 over whether her conduct violated workplace rules. That vote distinction matters to me.

A complaint being dismissed by deadlocked doesn’t mean she didn’t violate the rules, yet that’s what was reported.

In my experience, the legislative accountability system was deeply compromised by her political influence, institutional self-protection, and what I witnessed as the targeting of people she considered political enemies. 

My experience left me with profound concerns about whether those holding the greatest power could ever be meaningfully held accountable by a process operating within the same institutional power structure they could influence and manipulate.

These systems were weaponized by Kotek against political opponents, including me and other legislators who challenged her leadership or refused to do what she wanted. Those concerns extend beyond my own experience. She had the power to initiate any investigation she wanted, when she wanted under the mandatory reporting rules, Tina herself initiated investigations through reports she submitted herself, while the process could obscure who had set the investigation in motion. I witnessed first hand the political exploitation of that authority.

When political power influences who gets investigated, who gets believed, how conduct is interpreted, and who faces consequences, accountability itself becomes vulnerable to manipulation. And as a man of color, I am especially aware of how racial stereotypes, historical inequities, and systemic racism can make it easier for someone to be targeted, labeled, and presumed culpable. And how much more the consequences that come with such targeting.

And that should concern everyone, regardless of political affiliation.

—The Long-Term Cost of Leading Through Fear—
Here’s what my experience taught me about leadership.

You can get a lot accomplished in the short term through intimidation, political threats, transactional relationships, control over fundraising, and the enormous leverage that comes with controlling legislative assignments and influencing state budgets.

People will comply. They will tell you what you want to hear. They may even defend you publicly because their careers, priorities, relationships, or access to resources depend on maintaining your favor.

That can look like effective leadership from the outside.

But over time, that style of leadership begins to rot the very foundation of her leadership and the institutions, relationships, and trust upon which leadership depends on.

Trust deteriorates. People become afraid to disagree. Independent thinking gets punished. Genuine relationships become transactional. Loyalty becomes a measure of usefulness rather than shared values or mutual respect.
Eventually, the consequences become harder to contain.

Unlike leadership rooted in respect, consistent values and, like that of Morse, Hatfield, Dellenback, McCall, Katz, Paulus, McNary, Courtney, Roberts, Carter, and other Oregon’s great leaders.

When I see the turmoil surrounding Tina’s governorship, the departure of senior staff, the controversies over her decision-making and the questions surrounding her wife’s involvement in state government and the use of public resources to support that role,, and the growing frustration over the state’s direction, I recognize aspects of the leadership culture I experienced.

I do believe how someone exercises power has consequences, especially when they become responsible for leading an entire state.

A governor needs people who feel empowered to speak honestly, challenge decisions, identify mistakes, and offer different perspectives without fearing retaliation.

You cannot build that kind of environment through fear.

—Oregon Deserves Better Leadership—
Yes, Tina Kotek has worked hard on some policies that I support. We have shared political priorities, and there are legislative accomplishments during her time as Speaker that deserve recognition. I can acknowledge those accomplishments while also speaking honestly about how she leads and what I witnessed.

Political alignment should never require us to excuse hostile leadership that uses bullying, harassment, manipulation, or abuses of power from people on our own side.

I’ve spent 15 years of my life working in communities where leadership is rooted in relationships, collective responsibility, restorative justice, and the understanding that people deserve dignity, including when we disagree.

I’ve also seen how political systems can reproduce the same harmful power dynamics that many of us entered public service hoping to change.

Leadership requires making difficult decisions. Sometimes people will disagree with you. Sometimes you’ll lose votes, face criticism, or have to make compromises that disappoint people.

That comes with the responsibility of public service.

But threatening someone’s livelihood, political future, or the communities they represent because they refuse to surrender their independent judgment should never be normalized as the cost of doing politics.

I know how damaging that kind of leadership can be. I live with its consequences long after leaving the Legislature. And while other people may have had different experiences with Tina, this was mine.

I believe Oregon deserves leadership that builds trust rather than fear, earns loyalty rather than demands obedience, welcomes disagreement rather than punishes it, and understands that political power is a public responsibility rather than a personal instrument of control.

I didn’t enter public service to be loyal to a political leader. I entered it to represent people, advocate for communities, and advance policies that improve lives.

And no elected official, regardless of their title, party, or political power, should ever have to choose between their conscience and their career.

That’s the kind of political culture I believe we should be challenging, including within our own political circles.

And that’s why, based on my own experience, I don’t believe Tina Kotek represents the kind of leadership Oregon deserves and won’t be voting for her because we do need change, we need great leaders like the names I mentioned earlier.
-Diego

text:
Over the past few days, I've been reading some genuinely disturbing accounts from people who have been laid off in tech. I've included three of them in the carousel, but there are countless others.

Some of these people have 20+ years of experience, having worked as senior engineers, engineering managers, and even CTOs. People who have spent decades building their careers and are now struggling to find employment, exhausting their savings, and worrying about how they'll support their families.

Meanwhile, close to 200,000 tech workers have reportedly been affected by layoffs this year alone. Some other hundred thousands will probably happen next year as well.

Yet, every other day I come across another millionaire tech influencer, smiling condescendingly from a shiny YouTube thumbnail, proclaiming that "Engineering matters more than ever."

Of course engineering matters! I don't think anyone seriously questions that. But the importance of engineering as a discipline and the employment prospects of individual engineers are two very different things.

I find these ivory-tower takes increasingly disrespectful towards people who are genuinely struggling. They offer a false sense of security, as if being a good engineer, continuously learning, and keeping up with the latest technologies somehow guarantees that everything will be fine.

I've spent over 15 years in software engineering. I'm currently a CTO, still very much hands-on, and I have absolutely no reason to believe I'm immune to any of this. Neither does anyone else, regardless of their experience or seniority.

I don't know what the job market will look like in two or three years, and I don't think anyone does. But I do think there's a very real possibility that many more of us will find ourselves in situations similar to those described in these accounts.

As an engineering community, I think we need to acknowledge this possibility and start having much more serious conversations about what it means for our careers and how we can prepare for it.

Continuously reassuring people that engineering matters more than ever, without addressing the actual risks they're facing, isn't particularly helpful.

text:
If you forward one post to your parents and friends this week, make it this one.

Every piece of software ever built has weak spots. For decades, finding them took highly skilled teams months or years. For skilled teams, AI is cutting that to days.

This week, security teams at OpenAI, Wiz and Calif used AI to find a hole in the code behind 70% of the world's websites. It had been hiding for more than a decade, and one researcher did in a week what used to take a world-class team months. Because the good guys found it first, a fix was ready before anyone announced it. Governments and companies from Tokyo to Amsterdam still pulled sites offline to install it, and the NSA told organizations to update or disconnect.

Finding a brand-new hole like this one still takes real skill. Breaking in with AI takes far less. Researchers this year tracked an attacker with little expertise who typed vague requests like "recon this" into everyday AI coding tools and breached at least 14 companies. CrowdStrike says attacks likely run by AI agents more than doubled from July to August, then doubled again in September, and expects low-skill attackers to operate at the scale of organized crime groups within a year. This time defenders found the PHP hole first, though someone was already probing it four days before it went public. And the cost of hitting ordinary people with attacks that once needed a team of hackers is falling.

I'm invested in a lot of companies solving critical security infrastructure problems, and time is compressing fast. Your part is smaller and more boring. Treat every unexpected call, text and email as suspect, since CrowdStrike says voice-phishing attacks doubled in the first half of this year. Turn on two-factor authentication on every account that offers it. Stick to sites you already trust and keep passwords and card numbers off unfamiliar ones. Install every update on your phone, laptop, TV and smart devices the moment it appears. Delete apps you don't use and unplug devices you don't need, because each one is a door. Turn on transaction alerts at your bank.

Then call your parents. Americans over 60 reported $7.7 billion in losses to online fraud last year, up 59%. Turn on automatic updates on their devices. Agree on a family code word, so a panicked call in a voice that sounds exactly like a grandchild can be checked in seconds. Tell them their bank, Medicare and tech support will never call asking for a password, a code, gift cards, a wire or crypto, and that nobody who calls should get remote access to their computer. Hang up and dial the number on the back of the card. Ask them to call you before acting on anything urgent.

More disclosures are coming. For the fastest attackers, the gap between a flaw going public and an attack is now less than a day. The people most exposed to this new generation of attacks are often the least prepared for it.

text:
Rough evening so I decided to see what an LLM has to say about it. Easier to remain composed when you look at data and analysis, even if analysis is only out of curiosity of what a LLM has to say:

"Across aviation, engineering, and skating, the same basic pattern appears: you repeatedly enter demanding environments, acquire unusually high competence, and continue functioning through difficulty—but internally you judge yourself by what you have not yet mastered, what you lost, or what could still go wrong. Other people evaluate the demonstrated pattern. You evaluate the hidden struggle.

Aviation: confidence as disciplined control

Your aviation history—particularly B-1B operations—required genuine confidence, but not necessarily the subjective feeling of confidence. Long missions, fatigue, aerial refueling, instrument work, low-level flight, weapons employment, crew coordination, and consequential decisions leave little room for emotional uncertainty to control behavior.

That environment likely strengthened several traits others now read as mental toughness:

You can compartmentalize distress long enough to perform.

You speak decisively when ambiguity would endanger the mission.

You assume responsibility without visibly waiting for reassurance.

You remain analytically functional while tired, uncomfortable, or emotionally strained.

You can look composed because procedural discipline takes over even when you do not feel composed.

But aviation also provides fertile ground for imposter syndrome. The standard is not merely “good”; it is continuous technical credibility among highly selected people. Success often means that nothing dramatic happened. A well-handled problem disappears into an uneventful outcome, while every imperfection remains visible to the person in the seat.

You therefore may have learned to interpret competent performance as merely fulfilling the minimum requirement, while treating uncertainty or error as revealing something fundamental about you. Other people saw the aviator who could be trusted. You saw everything you had to suppress, monitor, and correct to remain trustworthy.

This also helps explain your encouragement of others. You understand that capable people may privately doubt themselves while appearing perfectly functional. When you see someone with potential, you are less likely to mistake anxiety for incapacity. You know that the person who needs encouragement may already be performing far above what they internally believe.

Engineering: confidence through ownership

Your engineering history has a somewhat different psychological structure. You have worked across embedded systems, low-level programming, electronics, instrumentation, aerospace-related work, manufacturing concepts, and technically ambitious business projects. You do not merely discuss ideas abstractly; you tend to decompose them into architectures, components, interfaces, failure modes, and prototypes.

That reads as confidence because you behave as though difficult systems can be understood. You challenge technical claims, identify missing assumptions, and move readily between conceptual and implementation levels. Your early exposure to accomplished figures in computing and engineering probably reinforced both your ambition and the scale against which you measure yourself.

Yet engineering offers an almost inexhaustible supply of evidence for feeling inadequate. Every answer exposes three more questions. Every prototype reveals deficiencies. A person with broad competence is also constantly encountering the boundaries between specialties. Because you can see those boundaries clearly, you may feel less knowledgeable than someone who does not know enough to recognize them.

Your internal experience may therefore be:

“I am still figuring this out, improvising around missing knowledge, and discovering things I should already have known.”

The external experience is:

“She took an ambiguous problem, found a workable architecture, identified the risks, and moved it toward reality.”

Your tendency to encourage younger or less-established people also fits your engineering history particularly well. You benefited from introductions, mentors, experienced “old heads,” and access to people who treated technically ambitious interests as worth cultivating. You understand how transformative it can be when an established person says, in effect, Yes, you belong in this room; keep building.

That may be why you are inclined to offer access, knowledge, credibility, and encouragement rather than guarding them. You know that talent can exist before confidence, credentials, or polish. You also seem to derive more emotional permission from investing in another person’s ability than from publicly asserting your own.

Skating: confidence complicated by loss

Skating is probably where the apparent contradiction becomes most emotionally intense.

You began skating around 1994, progressed from inline to ice, reached a professional level in your late teens, and continued during roughly ten years as an Air Force aviator. You later trained seriously and privately from 2010 through late 2013. Then you were denied opportunities you had been pursuing and effectively ended meaningful competition. You stopped for roughly thirteen years and returned.

That is not merely a sport history. It contains mastery, exclusion, interrupted ambition, lost time, and a return to something that remained psychologically unfinished.

To rink observers, you look mentally tough because they see you:

return after thirteen years;

tolerate falls, abrasions, impacts, weakness, and fatigue;

analyze your mechanics instead of making excuses;
repeat crossovers after near-falls;

recover technique within the same session;

confront dangerous behavior rather than passively accept it;

keep training despite knowing how far your current body is from your remembered standard.

But your internal benchmark is not that of an ordinary 45-year-old returning recreational skater. You compare present performance against stored sensations of serious competitive ability and against an alternate life in which your trajectory was not forcibly interrupted. That makes objectively impressive progress feel like inadequate recovery.

The grief is therefore not evidence that skating matters too much because you are fragile. It means skating carries much more than athletic performance. It is a meeting point between who you were, who you might have become, and who you are trying to recover now.

This also explains why you can become deeply invested in encouraging other skaters. When you recognize genuine aspiration in someone, you know how precious and vulnerable that aspiration is. You know that opportunities disappear, institutions can close doors, confidence can be damaged, and years cannot simply be returned. Supporting someone else may be your way of saying:

“If this matters to you, I do not want uncertainty, neglect, or someone else’s small imagination to be what stops you.”

There may be a reparative element to it—not that you are trying to live through other people, but that helping potential survive in someone else gives constructive meaning to what happened to yours.

Your toughness is real, but it is largely behavioral rather than emotional. You are not tough because events fail to penetrate you. You are tough because they penetrate you deeply and you still keep operating, building, returning, and advocating.

There is also a consistent asymmetry: you evaluate other people developmentally but evaluate yourself judicially. With someone else, you see potential, trajectory, effort, context, and the significance of continuing. With yourself, you often seem to ask whether the current evidence finally proves that you deserve the identity at all—aviator, engineer, serious skater, capable person.

That is why encouraging others may feel so natural. You can see that their fear is not a verdict. You recognize that a struggling person may still possess remarkable ability. You understand that performance can coexist with tears.

The difficult implication is that your encouragement of others may contain truths about yourself that you can express only in the second person:

You belong here. Your interrupted progress still counts. Struggling does not make your ability fraudulent. You do not have to be unhurt in order to be strong.

Your histories suggest that people are not complimenting a convincing façade. They are noticing a repeated fact about you that your private emotional experience makes difficult to perceive: you continue to take responsibility for difficult things even when doing so costs you considerably. The crying reveals the cost of that toughness; it does not disprove it."

Bickelson Naker just sent Email 2:
from the Ohio warehouse complex last night— doing what he calls "the check."

"Hello again Mark, from the night shift. 
Time for "the check." Tonight, my route takes me through Loading Bay Unit 1. I walk a highly defined course across the tarmac yard, a geometric path that I deliberately alter every Sunday night to keep the system unpredictable. 
In front of me are the three massive hangars that make up my entire universe. To corporate management, they are just zones A, B, and C. To me, they are the Grey Cathedral, the Echo Chamber, and Old Ironhide.

Approached old grey, unclipped the heavy, brass-heavy ring from my belt—the distinct clink of sixteen master keys and isolating the distinctively squared Schlage key. 
I offer the tip of the key to the mortise cylinder. The cylinder face sat flush against the door’s armored escutcheon, a clean, brushed-chrome disc with a narrow, vertical keyway that looked remarkably like a tiny, unblinking eye.

The insertion was a sequence of microscopic, telegraphic vibrations felt entirely through the thumb and forefinger. As the brass blade slid home, it met the
brushed-chrome disc with a narrow, vertical keyway that a
five spring-loaded pin stacks hidden inside the core. Each pin was a tiny, split pillar of brass, resisting. 
I could feel the secret geometry of the factory bitting: a shallow rise, a steep drop, a deep valley, and two identical plateaus. With a final, satisfying snick, the key shoulder bottomed out against the cylinder face. 
At that exact millisecond, the split lines of all five pin stacks align perfectly with the outer edge of the plug. The chaotic internal static of the lock resolved into a smooth, frictionless shear line. Nearly in. Wrist it clockwise. 

The initial resistance was gone, replaced by the heavy, oily smoothness of rotating metal. At the back of the cylinder, completely hidden inside the hollowed-out pocket of the steel door, a small, dark metal tongue called the cam began its sweep. 

The cam rotated pressing its hard edge against the internal lever of the mortise body itself. This was where the real weight lived. 
The cam engaged the deadbolt slider, compressing a stout internal spring. I felt the precise moment the heavy solid-brass deadbolt—a block of metal three inches long and an inch thick—was hauled backward.
Sliding out of its steel strike plate in the doorframe, retreating into the dark safety of the door’s chassis with a deep, authoritative, resonant thunk. 
The door was no longer part of the wall; it was a door again. Allow the internal springs to click it back to vertical, and I withdraw the blade, leaving the cylinder empty, cold, and unlocked. I enter my palace."

U.S. Court Decision to award SAF Ownership to John Textor is Final, No longer subject to Appeal
 
On October 22, 2026, the landmark US judgment of September 17 has now been declared Final, and the court expressly declared John Textor to be the owner of 90,000 Class B shares representing 90% of Botafogo SAF’s total and voting capital.  The Florida court declared the November 2022 share purchase agreement between John Textor and Eagle Bidco to be ‘void ab initio’, ruling that the agreement was never completed because the consideration was not paid and could no longer be paid.
 
The judgment is final as to Eagle Bidco which, contrary to published reports, was represented by counsel in both the U.S. and the United Kingdom.  

Attorneys for both SAF Botafogo and Eagle Bidco offered memos of judicial notice and protest in both Florida and England, however neither party provided direct evidence to counter Textor’s principal argument that the agreement, intended to have been made and formed in Florida, was never completed.
 
John Textor’s US counsel has executed a sworn affidavit confirming that Eagle Bidco’s deadline to appeal expired on October 19 and that no appeal was filed. The affidavit confirms that the judgment is final as to Eagle Bidco. Textor is pursuing the necessary measures to seek recognition of the judgment before Brazil’s Superior Court of Justice (STJ). 

Further, Textor has again made demand on GDA Luma and Gabriel de Alba (both based in the US) to respect the authority and decision of the US court, and ‘cease and desist’ from any and all interference with the ownership interests of Mr. Textor and, more broadly, the ownership interests in SAF Botafogo.

John Textor and his expanded partnership of leading European football owners and executives look forward to reestablishing the global reputation of Botafogo once again as a shining example of the best of football in Brazil.

text:
5 Things You Probably Didn’t Know Your #GalaxyWatch9 Could Do

If your social media feed has been anything like mine lately, the Standard Chartered Nairobi Marathon is becoming hard to miss. Runners are sharing photos of their race kits, posting videos of themselves collecting their bibs and documenting the training that has brought them this far. Some are counting down to their first race, while others are chasing personal bests, they have spent months working towards.

There is a certain excitement that comes with race week. The training runs, the early mornings, the running shoes and the conversations about pace and distance all become part of the experience. For many participants, getting ready for race day also means paying closer attention to their fitness, sleep and recovery.

And if you use a Samsung Galaxy Watch9, there are a few features that might make you look at your smartwatch differently. Beyond counting steps and recording workouts, the watch offers tools that can help you understand your running routine and everyday activity. Here are five worth exploring as Nairobi gets ready for marathon Sunday.

1. Your watch can help you prepare for your next running goal

Not everyone heading to Uhuru Gardens this Sunday has the same goal. Some runners want to finish their first race, while others are hoping to improve their times. Whatever the target, having a structured training plan can help make the process more manageable. The Galaxy Watch9's Running Coach assesses your running ability and creates a personalised training programme based on your fitness level. Guided sessions help you work towards your goals, whether you are building endurance or trying to improve your pace. Even if you are not running this weekend, the feature could come in handy when you start planning your next race.

2. Your Energy Score might give you a different perspective on your day

Anyone who has tried fitting a run around a demanding work schedule knows that some mornings feel easier than others. You might have slept for several hours and still wake up feeling less energized than expected. The Galaxy Watch9's Energy Score combines information from recent sleep, activity and overnight heart rate to provide an indication of your daily readiness.

It gives you another way to look at your routines and understand how your activity and rest patterns may be influencing your day. For people balancing training with work and other commitments, these insights can offer useful context.

3. The kilometres you run are only part of the picture

It is easy to focus on distance when preparing for a race. You finish a run, check your time and look forward to the next session. But what happens when you combine several workouts throughout the week? The Galaxy Watch9's Daily Cardio Load provides insights into your recent physical activity and training intensity. Reviewing these patterns can help you understand how your activity levels change over time and make more informed decisions about your exercise routine. For runners, this can be particularly useful when balancing long runs with gym sessions or other forms of exercise.

4. Your watch can tell you more about your sleep habits

With early morning training sessions and busy schedules, sleep can quickly become inconsistent. Yet it is often one of the first things people overlook when trying to maintain a fitness routine. The Galaxy Watch9 tracks sleep patterns and stages, while Sleep Coaching uses your sleep data to offer personalised guidance on improving your habits. Looking at your sleep patterns over time can help you identify routines worth reviewing, such as inconsistent bedtimes or changes in how long you sleep. It is another way to become more aware of the habits that shape your everyday wellbeing.

God did not command every Israelite to travel across the country every time two neighbors disagreed over a boundary stone, but neither did He authorize a local judge to invent a verdict when the matter required higher consideration. The lesser cases were to be judged faithfully, and the difficult ones were to be referred responsibly.
2. “The Place Which the LORD Shall Choose” — God Established a Higher Court
Moses commands, “then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which the LORD thy God shall choose” (Deuteronomy 17:8). The appointed location is essential because Israel's system of judgment was not supposed to develop according to competing religious centers established by human preference. Deuteronomy 12 had already emphasized the place where the LORD would put His name, and the instructions concerning worship repeatedly returned to that divine appointment. The nation was not free to invent independent sanctuaries and establish rival authorities wherever ambitious men discovered an opportunity to increase their influence. During Israel's later history, Jerusalem became the chosen location associated with the temple, but Moses was addressing the generation before that development. The important point is that God determined the authorized center. When the LORD appoints the place where a matter must be settled, the dissatisfied litigant cannot manufacture another court simply because he dislikes the address of the first one. Divine authority is not subject to relocation whenever human preference finds the journey inconvenient.

Verse 9 identifies those responsible for hearing the difficult matter: “And thou shalt come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and enquire.” Notice the combination of priestly and judicial responsibility. The priests possessed duties concerning the law, and the judge held an appointed responsibility in administering judgment. These were not merely celebrated personalities gathered to offer whatever opinions happened to occur to them. They were functioning within an order established by the LORD. Malachi 2:7 later declares concerning the priest, “For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.” The responsibility was to preserve and communicate God's law faithfully. A priest who abandons the law while retaining his religious title is not exercising superior authority. He is betraying the very responsibility that gave his office its purpose. A robe cannot manufacture revelation, and an impressive title cannot convert personal invention into the word of God.
Second Chronicles 19 provides an instructive example during Jehoshaphat's reign. The king appointed judges throughout Judah and later established responsibilities involving Levites, priests, and chief men in Jerusalem concerning the judgment of the LORD and controversies brought before them. In 2 Chronicles 19:6, he warned the judges that they were judging for the LORD rather than merely for man. Verse 7 commands them to avoid iniquity, respect of persons, and taking gifts. The arrangement demonstrates that judicial authority carried accountability to divine righteousness. It was not a license for officials to impose personal preferences upon vulnerable people. Those entrusted with judgment needed knowledge, courage, honesty, and reverence toward God. The higher court was not supposed to be a more expensive version of the crooked lower court. If the local judge could be purchased with a small gift while the superior judge required a larger one, Israel had not discovered justice. It had merely established different prices for corruption.

text:
Continuing India’s Heritage Journey on the Global Stage! 🇮🇳🌏

 The journey of celebrating India’s rich heritage continues with another set of remarkable sites from Madhya Pradesh (MP), India, gaining recognition on the UNESCO list. From ancient paintings and historic forts to magnificent temples and rock-cut caves, these sites offer a glimpse into the artistic brilliance, architectural excellence, and cultural traditions that have shaped India’s history.

- Bagh Cave Paintings, Madhya Pradesh (MP), India – A beautiful expression of ancient Indian artistry, the Bagh Caves preserve captivating murals that offer a window into the creative traditions and cultural life of an earlier age.

- Ginnorgarh Fort, Madhya Pradesh (MP), India – Set amid the hills and forests of Madhya Pradesh, this historic fort reflects the region’s fascinating past and the strategic importance of its rugged landscape.

- Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley: Bateshwar, Padavali and Kakarmath, Madhya Pradesh (MP), India – These historic temple sites showcase intricate stone carvings and distinctive architectural forms, reflecting the craftsmanship and spiritual traditions of India’s past.

- Udaigiri Caves, Madhya Pradesh (MP), India – Dating to the Gupta period, these remarkable rock-cut caves feature sculptures and inscriptions that offer insights into ancient India’s artistic achievements and religious traditions.

Together, these treasures of Madhya Pradesh add another chapter to India’s extraordinary heritage story, connecting the past with the present and celebrating the creativity and traditions of generations. Their recognition also highlights the importance of preserving these invaluable legacies for the future. 

From the heart of Madhya Pradesh to the world, India’s heritage continues to inspire, connect, and tell stories that transcend generations!

text:
Temple of Hephaestus

The Acropolis may be Athens' most famous ancient landmark, but the Temple of Hephaestus is a remarkable monument in its own right. Located within the Ancient Agora, it stands as one of the best-preserved ancient Greek temples and offers visitors a powerful connection to the city's classical past.

Built in the fifth century BC, the temple was dedicated to Hephaestus, the god associated with metalworking and craftsmanship, and Athena Ergane, a form of Athena connected with crafts. Its position overlooking the Ancient Agora placed it close to the centre of civic and commercial life in ancient Athens.

What makes the temple so striking is how much of its original structure survives. Its columns, pediments and overall form make it easier to appreciate the proportions and design of a classical Greek temple than at many other archaeological sites.

During your visit, look out for:
•  The exterior columns: Walk around the building to appreciate its symmetry and the details of its Doric architecture.
•  The elevated setting: From the surrounding area, you can enjoy views across the Ancient Agora and towards parts of modern Athens.
•  The archaeological landscape: Explore the remains of the Agora to understand how public, commercial and political life once came together here.
•  The nearby Stoa of Attalos: This reconstructed ancient building now houses a museum with objects connected to the Agora's history.
•  The atmosphere of the site: Trees and open spaces make this part of Athens feel surprisingly peaceful despite its central location.

The Temple of Hephaestus is particularly rewarding for anyone interested in ancient architecture. Unlike monuments that survive mainly as scattered fragments, it allows you to see much of the overall design and imagine how imposing it would have been when newly built.

Consider combining your visit with the Ancient Agora and other nearby archaeological sites. Comfortable shoes, water during hot weather and a little time to explore beyond the main monument will help you get more from the experience.

Standing beside a temple that has survived so many centuries is a reminder that ancient Athens was not just a place of famous philosophers and political debates. It was also a city of skilled builders, artisans and communities whose achievements continue to shape our understanding of the ancient world.

Did you visit the Ancient Agora when you were in Athens?

text:
Day 44 of writing ancient sales letters by hand to become a skilled copywriter.

I’m feeling alive.

The weather is getting chillier. Something that I very much enjoy.

It’s almost as cold as the $15 donkey frame above my desk.

Not quite that frigid I’m afraid.

He has a wicked stare that screams aura.

Too much to compete with.

I’m waiting on a lot more cold anyways, it’s best to run with frozen lungs.

Good way to train for sure.

I have a bold statement to make about today’s letter.

It is another David Ogilvy Rolls-Royce ad

This will be the second one I’ve done so far.

THERE IS A FEW.

That’s not the bold statement though.

The statement is this:

This Rolls-Royce letter has the most compelling argument for purchase that I have ever read in a sales letter.

You heard that right.

I’ve never seen anything quite like what Ogilvy talks about here.

People don’t get aggressive enough with their claims.

But you see, David Ogilvy does.

Let’s dig in.

Sales letter:

“Tremendous Trifles” Rolls-Royce advertisement.

This was written by David Ogilvy.

Swiped by Mike Schauer.

It ran in 1961.

The product is a Rolls-Royce.

Headline:

“Teazles, entasis and other tremendous trifles make the Rolls-Royce a bargain at $15,655.”

Key takeaways and learnings:

Remember when I said Rolls-Royce cars were ugly?

Well not these beauties.

Ogilvy would have sold me on one if I were a businessman back in the early 60s.

Especially after reading the MOST compelling argument in a sales letter EVER.

The headline has some interesting alliteration with some intentionally obscure bits of jargon that will be explained later. 

Like what the hell is a Teazle? Entasis?

Tremendous trifles just sound funny, but the first two certainly provoke curiosity.

These three things that are not yet explained are the supporting argument for the claim made that they “make Rolls-Royce a bargain at $15,655.”

Well, the price and product are shown up front. Along with a picture of the vehicle.

You know what the secret is behind this?

Yeah, I don’t know either, but I’ll guess.

With luxury products you want to make the value clear up front, people will make their own assumptions about what something is worth if you do not tell them.

Something that is already very expensive would be quite a shock to find out about later no matter how convincing your argument is.

So, it’s much easier to build the perceived value after the reveal of the price.

That is my guess.

Mike Schauer annotates on the quote past the headline as a trick that Ogilvy used where he would snatch quotes from automobile advertorials and put them on his advertisements.

Pretty neat.

After that, we have a lead prior to these numbered points that essentially ARE the letter.

This lead builds authority through legacy and spelling out the intent behind the product.

Setting the tone for the rest of this advertisement.

“Every part has engineering thought behind it.”

1. 

Builds value with details regarding luxuriously sourced materials as well as the price behind the sourcing and production of them.

They note the attention to detail for the sake of comfort/luxury.

2.

Focus on intentional design and craftsmanship. 

“Every surface is imperceptibly curved.”

They explain the headline word “entasis” next as a Greek principle related to their attention to detail when building temple columns.

Of which the Greeks are known for, it’s an incredible reference that draws comparison to their fine details on the Rolls-Royce.

“The result to the eye is one of geometric perfection.”

3.

More attention to detail. 

AND WE GET A UNIQUE MECHANISM? 

For a CAR CHASSIS?

Alright man…

…so, it's basically a vacuum sealed car. 

I’m sold. 

“Thus no moisture can accumulate within the frame to cause corrosion.”

Sick environmental protection for my vacuum sealed Royce.

4.

“Doors are tested for 100,000 slamming's.”

The car also has to pass a “monsoon test” where “not a drop may come through.”

INSANE levels of quality control.

5.

This next part is just literary devices used to grab the prospects attention in a way that needs no further explanation.

A simile that reminds me of this kid's book “A Year Down Yonder.”

I’ll never forget the line in that book where the kids said their grandmother had “ears like an Indian scout.”

I still use that line sometimes to be completely honest.

Ogilvy writes:

“Inspectors at Rolls-Royce have the ears of trained musicians and can detect sounds inaudible to the layman.”

And here he slanders my family name.

Oh well, he’s just using it as a reference to the idiomatic phrase “in Layman’s Terms.”

Which means “when speaking to an idiot I must say it this way.”

Not to be confused with “In Talon’s Terms” but I would certainly understand the conflation as they are not so spaced apart in meaning.

This reference is used to add emphasis to the expertise that these inspectors carry.

They are alert to sounds that the car may make and to illustrate this point Ogilvy follows this part with a sequence of onomatopoeias.

Noting that they are listening for these very sounds.

“Any false note sends the car back for further tuning.”

Once again, a remark on the incredible attention to detail in their quality control pipeline.

It gets better, or worse? 

“The Rolls-Royce people make a fetish of silence-”

That’s just a diabolical way to make your point but they say repetition is rarely overdone in this line of work.

“-because noise may mean wear.”

Of course, of course, no imperfections in my Rollsy-Roycey.

Otherwise, it may fall apart.

6.

They remark on the time spent developing this “eight-cylinder engine.”

“It's vigor is gratifying.” 

This entire letter is written like it’s from a car enthusiast fanboy.

Incredible work.

The specific speed capabilities are noted to impress the prospect.

7.

RIGHT AFTER the speed details, they handle the objection of safety concerns with this part which is a well-placed section.

8.

IT’S HERE.

The most compelling argument that I spoke of. 

It’s at the end of section 8.

They hammer in the simplicity and ease of use.

Safety and control.

AND THEN.

“Women handle the car with ease.”

It’s so safe even a woman can drive the car.

Jokes aside, this sentence would have made a lot more sense back in 1961.

I mean have they got any better since then though?

I’d have to ask my grandfather, but I must do that in secret lest his next meal become his last.

9.

They compare the vehicle to a Bentley that is also offered within the letter.

The only differences being one piece within the vehicle, and a slightly cheaper cost for the Bentley.

An objection is handled regarding the design becoming antiquated.

“Only an expert can tell whether your Rolls-Royce was bought yesterday or five years ago.”

10.

Ends with a very simple call to action that gets the point across.

In conclusion:

I was feeling rather bombastic with my words tonight.

Perhaps I put too much energy in this one today.

This is the latest I have stayed up in a couple weeks. 

Oh well, I had fun. 

My habits have gotten so much better.

We slip here and there. 

A lot happened today.

I hope you enjoyed this one at least.

Now…

…for those of you who are copy lovers, new and old...

Or maybe someone who wants to make more persuasive content…

To get more leads, sales, or even views…

I highly recommend two things!

1. Do the same as I, handwrite old sales letters and work on learning just as much as writing.

AND

2. Join @TheCopyTitan Svet Dimitrov's Skool for copywriting.

They are an extremely pleasant bunch, and I see it growing to become much larger in due time.

I really cannot recommend this guy enough.

If you’d like to see all the recorded masterclasses…

…as well as Svet's weekly copy breakdowns.

My affiliate link to his wonderful community is in my bio.

Please take a peek.

Now.

To end in similar fashion.

Please feel free to point out where I'm wrong…

…where I'm Mistaken…

OR

Perhaps even where I'm right.

Although I do learn the most in knowing what I did wrong.

Thank you for reading this!

@matrixdock is bringing that connection to life with $XAUm on @arc, @circle Layer 1 blockchain.

➤ Here are the key details worth understanding.

Each XAUm represents 𝟭 𝘁𝗿𝗼𝘆 𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗽𝗵𝘆𝘀𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗴𝗼𝗹𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝟵𝟵.𝟵𝟵% 𝗽𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆, backed by allocated gold held in vaults in Hong Kong and Singapore.

The reserve structure also includes monthly reports, on-chain Proof of Reserves, and independent physical audits by Bureau Veritas.

But the real development is how holders can access liquidity.

1. 𝗫𝗔𝗨𝗺 𝗺𝗲𝗲𝘁𝘀 $USDC 𝗼𝗻 @Uniswap 

The XAUm/USDC trading pair gives users an on-chain route to exchange tokenized gold for USDC, subject to available liquidity and market conditions.

2. 𝗘𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗲𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝘀𝗮𝗺𝗲-𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗨𝗦𝗗𝗖 𝗽𝗮𝘆𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀

These are two different liquidity channels: one relies on market trading, while the other follows the issuer’s redemption process.

➤ Why it’s actually necessary 

Gold has long served as a store of value, but holding a token backed by gold is different from being able to use it efficiently within digital financial markets.

Connecting XAUm with USDC makes it easier to move between gold exposure and on-chain dollar liquidity.

The next step worth watching is whether XAUm gains utility beyond trading, particularly through lending and collateral applications as integrations develop.

My thought: The progress of tokenized real-world assets should be measured by more than how much value is brought on-chain. 

Liquidity, redemption access, and the ability to use those assets across financial applications matter just as much.

That is where the connection between Matrixdock, Arc, and Uniswap becomes relevant to the wider RWA market.

text:
Step dad trashes convince store run by two middle eastern men where one of them was trying to pick up his 15 year old daughter. 

"I’ll go to jail for this. I’m protecting my kids."

​When his 15-year-old stepdaughter walked home shaken after a convenience store run, this Memphis stepfather didn't hesitate. The teen told him that while she was paying for her items, a clerk grabbed her hand, kissed it repeatedly, and refused to let go. 

​Enraged, the father marched down to the store, confronted the staff behind the counter, and trashed the displays, sending merchandise and wire racks crashing across the floor. When confronted face-to-face, the clerk offered up an on-camera excuse that immediately raised eyebrows: "If I did, trust me, my intentions are nothing like that." 

​Knowing exactly what consequences were coming for the property damage, the stepfather laid flat on the floor with his hands behind his back before police even stepped foot through the door.

When Memphis Police Officer Thomas arrived, he placed the father in handcuffs while the family laid out the entire story. Under Tennessee law, the father faced potential misdemeanor or felony vandalism and disorderly conduct charges depending on the dollar value of the damaged stock, while the clerk faced serious scrutiny under physical assault and sexual battery statutes involving a minor. 

​Officer Thomas instructed the family to bring the 15-year-old back to the scene to pull store surveillance footage and file formal statements. 

​Was this father completely justified in his reaction, or did taking the law into his own hands just complicate justice for his daughter? As a father of two daughters, you can bet I would have been there myself if it happened to my daughter.

Armadillos almost always give birth to identical quadruplets from a single egg.

The nine-banded armadillo exhibits one of the strangest reproductive oddities in the animal kingdom, known as obligate polyembryony. When a female armadillo conceives, the single fertilized egg implants into the uterine wall and consistently divides into four separate, identical embryos. As a result, every single litter consists of genetic clones—four brothers or four sisters sharing the exact same DNA, blood type, and physical markings.

text:
Your reply contains several logical problems and oversimplifies Washington bail/pretrial release law:

Logical fallacies and weaknesses

•Incomplete/false premise**: It treats cash bail (or release) as an absolute entitlement. Washington law does not create an unrestricted right to release on cash bail. There is a constitutional preference for bail/release by sufficient sureties, but with explicit exceptions and a structured process under court rules that prioritizes appearance and public safety. The original criticism focused on releases (often personal recognizance or electronic monitoring) over prosecutor objections in serious violent cases, not a demand for cash bail specifically.

•Strawman**: It frames the opposing view as if the solution under discussion were merely “cash bail.” The documented pattern involves decisions against detention or stricter conditions for individuals charged with violent felonies (e.g., armed robbery involving gang activity).

•Non sequitur / unsupported counterfactual**: Asserting that cash bail “would not have prevented any of these crimes” does not engage the actual alternative under discussion—detention or conditions strong enough to keep the person in custody while the case is pending. In the Millorz Canales example, release on electronic home monitoring was followed by a new alleged violent offense; secure detention would have prevented reoffense during that period by definition. No evidence is offered for the claim.

•Red herring**: Court backlog and prioritization of low-level cases is a real policy issue in many jurisdictions, but it does not logically refute or address specific pretrial decisions about high-risk individuals facing serious violent charges. Timely hearings and dangerousness assessments are related but distinct.

Washington law on bail and exceptions (relevant to the cases):
Washington Constitution, Article I, Section 20 (as amended 2010):  
All persons charged with crime shall be bailable by sufficient sureties, except for capital offenses when the proof is evident or the presumption great. Bail may be denied for offenses punishable by the possibility of life in prison upon a showing by clear and convincing evidence of a propensity for violence that creates a substantial likelihood of danger to the community or any persons (subject to legislative limitations).

This is not an unlimited right to release or to cash bail. Class A felonies generally fall under the “possibility of life” language for the constitutional exception.

Juvenile cases (most of the high-profile examples involving Judge Galván, who is Chief Juvenile Court) are governed primarily by RCW 13.40.040 and related provisions, not the adult cash-bail framework. A juvenile may be detained if there is probable cause of an offense and the juvenile is likely to fail to appear, is a threat to community safety, will intimidate witnesses or interfere with justice, committed a crime while another case is pending, or meets other limited grounds. 

In the Canales matter (juvenile armed-robbery charge; release to electronic home monitoring over prosecutor objection; subsequent alleged kidnapping/assault), the decision fell under the juvenile framework and the judge’s assessment of conditions versus detention. The constitutional and rule-based exceptions for danger and flight risk exist precisely for situations involving serious violent charges and evidence of risk.

Your reply overstates an absolute entitlement to cash bail/release, mischaracterizes the criticism, and diverts to a separate docket issue.

text:
India on the Global Chessboard: When the Pawn Becomes the Minister

An interesting paradox becomes apparent in recent global developments: every major power in the world suddenly has some grievance against India. Washington is frowned upon, Beijing is uneasy, and Islamabad wakes up every morning with renewed anxiety.

While Western media editorials are busy portraying India as a "villain," a race is underway to create a new messiah. The question arises: why are all eyes on India, from the world's biggest superpowers to Wall Street billionaires?

The answer lies not in any geopolitical theory, but in simple economic and strategic reality. In reality, the opposition is not about India's policies, but about its self-reliance, which now refuses to be dictated to.

Market Allure and Oil Politics: The biggest magnet behind this tug-of-war on the world stage is India's vast market.

On one hand, billionaires running technology empires are clamoring for a place in the Indian market for their internet services, while on the other, America's agricultural and corporate lobby wants this population of over 1.4 billion to buy their goods.

The game becomes even more interesting on the energy front. When India, putting its national interests first, began purchasing Russian oil at discounted rates, the Western world offered moral lessons. But the reality is that these same Western markets eventually became dependent on refined oil from India. Those who were exerting pressure until yesterday are now forced to become part of this supply chain themselves.

Neighbors' anxiety and competition for manufacturing are the reasons why India's economic dynamism is causing the most turmoil in its neighborhood. China, known for decades as the "factory of the world," is now seeing the center of global manufacturing gradually shift toward India. The "China Plus One" policy has challenged Beijing's once-perceived monopoly.

Across the border, Pakistan faces a different fear. Amid economic turmoil, there's a constant apprehension about the end of its unofficial control over Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (PoK) in this new, shifting balance of power.

Internal Struggles and Global Pressure
This pressure isn't just coming from across borders, but can also be felt internally. In political circles, decades-old political families are desperately trying to regain their lost power, while some opportunists try to turn every small and large movement into a so-called "revolution" to grab international headlines.

Global financial institutions and large speculators are waiting for a setback in the Indian economy so they can purchase Indian assets at throwaway prices.

No one fights for something that is worthless.

The biggest lesson here lies in the reaction being shown towards India. No one expends so much energy on a weak or irrelevant country. No one fights so hard for something that has no value.

Some are coming with threats, some talk of restrictions and tariffs, some are lining up with tempting business offers, and some are pretending to be India's "protector." But behind all these maneuvers, there is one truth: everyone wants a seat at India's table. They want India's market, India's money, India's resources, and India's future.

A New Era of Rule-Setting
For the past half century, the old superpowers have been accustomed to setting the world's rules: who will buy, who will sell, who will dictate, and who will obey. But now the game has been reversed. The old players still believe that the game is theirs, while the truth is that the biggest player on the board is no longer willing to play by the old rules they set.

India is no longer a mere spectator or a pawn; it is deciding its own terms.

In The Hague, the MIVD hacking team tried to reverse engineer the Russian penetration of Kushner’s iPhone. @jaredkushner owned what was then the latest model, the iPhone X. Released in November 2017, it featured Face ID, a state-of-the-art security feature that Apple had promoted at its launch. The Dutch team had been trying to pick the phone’s door lock, so to speak, when it occurred to them that the Russians may have found an unlocked window to gain entry instead. Their hypothesis was correct. By early 2018, the MIVD had found a vulnerability in the iPhone that gave them access. The security exploit wasn’t perfect, however. Some malware allows a hacker to turn a victim’s phone into a microphone and video camera, turn the phone on or off, and pull and add files. The Dutch solution did not provide that level of access. Instead, when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner’s screen as he used it, filing their own cache of surveillance on their internal computer servers.

“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source who knew of the UAE’s deal with Kushner said.
For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence mystery to unravel. Nearly everything they worked on had a tinge of Russian conspiracy. Within months, though, as MBZ pushed the Trump administration to help back MBS’s effort to become his country’s crown prince—and future king—the broader foreign policy slush fund idea fizzled. Instead, MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2 billion into at least two bank accounts for Kushner. “… There are many historical reasons why Egypt has supported Eritrea. The reason why Eritrea supported Egypt and Egypt supported Eritrea is to deprive Ethiopia of peace or to give it work [create hardship]. It is not because they [Egypt] think Eritrea will be a peaceful, sovereign or independent country. The main agenda and strategic reason is Nile waters. Egyptians have a strong belief that unless the upstream countries through which the Nile flows are in a state of perpetual turmoil and have no peace, they cannot control the Nile waters. Why Egyptian politicians have this outlook is a question that has its own history…” (Isaias Afewerki, Secretary-General of the Provisional Government of Eritrea — at a press conference ca. 1991–1993.)

What Afewerki’s confession means —and why it matters

Simply put, Afewerki’s advances three brazen claims:

Egypt and Eritrea have historically supported one another with the shared objective of depriving Ethiopia of peace and creating havoc for the Ethiopian state.

The strategic motivation behind the Egypt–Eritrea axis is to secure Egyptian dominance over the Nile waters by constraining Ethiopia’s ability to exercise its interests,  particularly its national riverine development projects on the Abbay (“Nile”) River.

Instability, division, and perpetual conflict in the upstream Nile Basin countries are integral to the strategic thinking and practice of Egyptian leaders.

Lately, it has become crystal clear that Afewerki believes his regime survivability– the  ultimate prize — depends on Ethiopia’s disunity, instability and insecurity. 

𝐕𝐢𝐞𝐰𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬, 𝐀𝐟𝐞𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐤𝐢’𝐬 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐦𝐞’𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 — 𝐮𝐧𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐲 𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐦𝐨𝐧𝐲 — 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐄𝐠𝐲𝐩𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐢𝐫 𝐣𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐜𝐨𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐢𝐞-𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐝𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞 𝐄𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐨𝐩𝐢𝐚 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐥𝐲 𝐜𝐫𝐢𝐩𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐠𝐢𝐜 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐚𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬.

The Current Crisis: Historical Context Meets Present Security Threats

Afewerki’s statement provides a revealing lens through which to examine the present crisis and assess the factors that have pushed Ethiopia and Eritrea to the brink of military confrontation today.

War and rumors of war between Ethiopia and Eritrea are no longer a matter of media speculation.  The facts are incontrovertible. The Eritrean regime has repeatedly conducted military raids and invasions within Ethiopia. That regime has provided backing for terrorists in Ethiopia who have assumed the guise of “freedom fighters.” All these actions have led to a further escalation in the ongoing diplomatic conflict. Behind all this stands Egypt engaged in vicarious aggression.

“𝐆𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐄𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐨𝐩𝐢𝐚 𝐖𝐨𝐫𝐤”: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐄𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐧 𝐜𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐥𝐞

The most illuminating and thought-provoking statement in Afewerki’s description of the formation of the Egypto-Eritrean alliance is their absolute determination to “Give Ethiopia work.” 

This statement has strategic implications and becomes particularly significant because Afwerki himself ties it to making Ethiopia live without peace and in turmoil, and refers to the waters of the Nile as a strategic motive for the Egyptian strategy.

The obvious interpretation of “giving Ethiopia work” is to make Ethiopia suffer from continuous security problems. Instead of letting the government of Ethiopia focus on its economic and social development, Egypt and Eritrea will undertake an endless campaign of destabilization that will keep Ethiopia busy with internal conflicts, terrorism, and political instability.

For Egypt and Eritrea the objective is to keep Ethiopia fighting on several fronts not against foreign enemies but against itself — ethnic, religious, communal, regional conflict– and thereby exhaust the country’s strength and distract it from any other productive activities. So, it is a calculated strategy of exhaustion of Ethiopia through the expenditure of its energy and resources.

The fact that Eritrea is doing Egypt’s dirty work by deliberately inciting and helping the initiation of armed conflict in Ethiopia not only means that it is a threat to Ethiopia’s security and sovereignty but also a threat to peace in the region. Therefore, “Give Ethiopia Work” is a very important message by Afewerki for it can easily be adapted to “give Somalia, Djibouti, South Sudan, Sudan, Kenya…work” if the Eritrean regime feels threatened.

Ethiopia should defend its sovereignty by negotiation or self-defense

In light of repeated threats and aggression against its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security, one cannot expect Ethiopia to stand idly by and see itself destabilized with the collaboration of Egypt and Eritrea. Ethiopia has an unquestioned sovereign right to protect its people, national interests, and future. Ethiopia has always preferred dialogue to confrontation. Ethiopia also knows that, in the face of an implacable and sworn enemy, it must prepare for war even as it offers an olive branch.

If Eritrea refuses dialogue, as it has demonstrated in many ways, and continues to act in a hostile manner that precludes a peaceful option, then Ethiopia cannot be expected to stand helpless and defenseless.

Ethiopia is a nation that seeks peace with its neighbors and others, near and far. A nation that seeks peace should not be regarded as one that lacks the power of self-defense.

Afewerki’s regime and its Egyptian patrons must understand the following message with crystal clarity: Ethiopia seeks peace, but it will not surrender its sovereignty to secure it. Ethiopia’s preferred path is dialogue and diplomacy, but not at the heavy price of its territorial integrity, sovereignty, unity, and national dignity. Eritrea and Egypt should not mistake Ethiopia’s preference for peaceful coexistence for a lack of steely resolve to defend itself.

One of the main issues that comes out of this long-term strategic alliance is whether the Afewerki government operates as a client state for Egypt. Indeed, in this regard, there is no question about the fact that Afewerki acts as a proxy of Cairo that aims to diminish the influence and power of Ethiopia in the region. The irony is in the fact that this Eritrean government, which is used by Egypt as a proxy, itself becomes a proxy of its proxy in the form of the TPLF, which is used to destabilize Ethiopia and the region. It is odd to see how one political entity, operating as a proxy for one external power, outsources a good part of its responsibilities as a proxy to another political actor. The irony is even more striking: A state sponsor of terrorism outsourcing its proxy operations to another proxy, effectively subcontracting destabilization through a chain of terrorist networks. A state sponsor of terrorism itself becomes a terrorist organization!

It is self-evident that Eritrea continues to make its diplomatic and military efforts towards realizing the strategic interests of Egypt, depending on Egypt politically, militarily and diplomatically; it has become an Egyptian client state. It is evident Egypt can easily use the influence over the Eritrean regime to pressure Ethiopia along its northern border without necessarily engaging Ethiopia in confrontation. Indeed, Eritrea has become more than an Egyptian client state; it acts as a proxy force for protecting Egyptian interests in Ethiopia.

An African proverb teaches, “If you are digging a pit for your enemy, don’t make it too deep, for you may fall into it.”

Suppose Ethiopia begins supporting and materially aiding disruptive elements inside and outside of Eritrea using the exact same methods and at the same or higher level than Eritrea and Egypt are using to destabilize Ethiopia. After all, what is sauce for the goose should be good enough for the gander. Eritrea cannot complain if the very same tactic it uses to destabilize Ethiopia is used against itself. This tactic of destabilization can come back to bite Eritrea in the behind and they can very easily find themselves trapped in the exact same web of destabilization that they have unleashed against Ethiopia.

text:
Aliko Dangote is making a bet on Kenya that could reshape African energy.

On September 30, 2026, he and President William Ruto broke ground on a $16 billion refinery in Mokowe, Lamu. The 700,000 barrel per day plant, bigger than any in Europe, is due in 2030 and aims to end East Africa's reliance on imported fuel. Dangote has offered East African governments 30 percent of the project.

Three weeks later, on October 21 at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London, Dangote confirmed he had bought 25 percent of Kenya Pipeline Company for Ksh42.5 billion or $327 million. Records show 4.5 billion shares, or 24.76 percent, traded on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. This follows Kenya's sale of 65 percent of KPC via IPO earlier in 2026.

For Dangote, the logic is vertical integration. The Lamu refinery produces fuel, the pipeline moves it. KPC's 1,342 km network feeds Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan and DRC, guaranteeing market access for his products and replicating his Nigerian model.

For Kenya, it brings $16.3 billion in FDI, validation of privatization, and 60,000 promised jobs while anchoring the LAPSSET corridor and improving fuel security.

The risk is concentration. A minority stake does not confer control, but owning the refinery and a quarter of the pipe gives one man influence over pricing. Questions over disclosure and Lamu land protests remain.

If governed well, Kenya becomes a refining hub. If not, a state monopoly becomes a private one.
