text:
Fulfilling purpose must be the primary goal of every person.

You're the way you are because of why you are.

Have you ever sat down to ask yourself why you are here and what you are meant to contribute to this world?

We are all different for a reason. 

We have different gifts, different experiences, different opportunities, and different paths to follow.

The problem is that many people spend so much time trying to become like others that they forget to discover who they are and what they were created to do.

You don't have to live another person's life to prove that you are successful. 

You don't have to follow somebody else's timeline to prove that you are making progress.

Learn from people, celebrate their success, and allow their achievements to inspire you. 

But never become so distracted by their journey that you abandon yours.

The goal is not just to make money, become popular, or acquire everything this world has to offer. 

The goal It is also to discover your purpose and make meaningful use of the life God has given you.

Imagine spending your whole life trying to be someone else, only to realise that you never gave yourself the opportunity to become who you were meant to be.

Don't let that be your story.

Discover yourself. 

Develop your gifts. 

Keep learning, keep growing, and keep working towards the things that truly matter.

You were not born to compete with everybody. 

You were born to fulfil your purpose.

text:
Late autumn settles quietly over Hainan — not with frost, but with flavor.
Crabs arrive plump and rich, the coast offers its freshest catch, and the northern wind does its quiet work, drying the harvest of sea and field. By the eaves, chrysanthemums bloom; on the table, chrysanthemum cake is savored. Taro simmers, coconut soups soothe the autumn dryness, and prayers rise for health and peace in the year ahead.
Out in the fields, migratory birds return to the rice paddies. On the hills, people climb to watch clouds drift across the sky.
Frost may not reach this island — but autumn does, in every taste and every view.

text:
Jackson says Homeward JXN faces $5 million shortfall for rehousing plan

Jackson city officials announced a funding shortfall for Homeward JXN, the city’s planned rehousing initiative, saying they now need another $5 million to fully fund the program in Jackson. City leaders had previously committed about $3.1 million in HOME American Rescue Plan Act funds and expected additional support from the Mississippi Home Corporation (MHC), but MHC told city officials it would provide far less than anticipated.

Chronology provided by city officials and MHC shows the city identified roughly $3.1 million in ARPA HOME funds for the program and expected MHC to match that amount. MHC officials later informed city staff that the agency could offer up to $500,000 for support services and $250,000 for tenant-based rental assistance, in the form of reimbursable grants, and that Jackson’s application remained under review.

City planning and program descriptions state Homeward JXN aims to house about 300 chronically homeless people over two years and provide services to roughly 1,100 additional people who enter homelessness during that period. Officials estimated the full program would cost about $10 million, including rent support, caseworkers, and program administration; the city has begun outreach to businesses and foundations to close the gap.

City officials say they plan to launch test sites this fall and have identified a first encampment for rehousing work; MHC’s stated funding limits and the reimbursable nature of its grants are documented by the agency as factors affecting immediate program financing. The city’s application to MHC was described as still under review.

🚨Tencent is building “Penguin Island” — a city-sized HQ on reclaimed land in Shenzhen for up to 80,000 people. Offices, apartments, schools, autonomous shuttles & more. 809,000 m² site, 3M+ m² floor space. Named after their penguin mascot.

🚨Centerpiece of Penguin Island: Tencent Helix. Nearly twice the size of Apple Park (~500,000 m²), designed as a vortex of spiraling towers around a central incubator. Due ~2028.

🚨Tencent’s Shanghai campus (East China HQ / Binjiang Tower) is a 150m, 29-story landmark. Pixelated “twinkling lights” facade inspired by a Chinese proverb. LEED Gold, workout spaces on every floor.

🚨Founded 1998 in the Cayman Islands. First product was OICQ (QQ after ICQ lawsuit). Unprofitable for first 3 years — then became one of China’s biggest companies.

🚨In 2001, South African media firm Naspers invested ~$32M for ~46.5% of Tencent. One of the greatest investments in history — returns in the thousands of times.

🚨Tencent is the world’s largest gaming company by revenue. Owns Riot Games (League of Legends) 100%, major stake in Epic (Fortnite), controls most of Supercell (Clash of Clans).

🚨WeChat is a true super-app used by 1B+ people. Messaging + payments + mini-apps + social + services all in one. Essential daily infrastructure in China.

🚨Name “Tencent” comes from Chinese “Tengxun” (腾讯) — roughly “galloping message.” Incorporates founder Pony Ma’s name. Penguin mascot originated with QQ.

🚨Tencent has invested in hundreds of companies (Tesla, Spotify, Discord, and many more) while building its own massive platforms in social, payments, cloud, and AI (Hunyuan).

🚨First Asian tech company to hit $500B valuation (2018). Still one of China’s most valuable firms, powered by gaming, WeChat, fintech, and ads.

🚨Earlier Shenzhen towers already had skybridges with a running track, sports facilities, and robot guides — a preview of the full “city” approach at Penguin Island.

🚨Penguin Island offers subsidized sea-view apartments, schools, and open public spaces. Built to retain talent in a nearly self-contained tech district.

text:
CorridorKey 2 Enhances Green Screen Removal

It’s that time of the week when we dive into some fresh tech news and today, it's all about CorridorKey 2. This update from Corridor Crew aims to make green screen removal a breeze for video editors. But does it really live up to the hype? Let’s find out.
CorridorKey 2 Enhances Green Screen Removal

CorridorKey 2 is an advanced tool designed specifically for removing green screens and blue screens in videos. It leverages sophisticated AI techniques to predict masks (matte layers) and clean foregrounds for each frame, making it easier to handle complex scenes that traditional chroma keying often struggles with.
How Does CorridorKey 2 Work?

The magic behind CorridorKey 2 lies in its ability to process video input and generate accurate predictions. It offers three hint modes:
• No Hint: The model decides what to cut out on its own.
• First-Frame Hint: A guide based on the first frame of the video.
• Full-Hint Video: A full video guide for each frame.

This flexibility allows users to tailor the tool’s output according to their specific needs, whether they’re working with simple or complex scenes. For instance, if you're dealing with a scene where the subject moves significantly from one frame to another, using the Full-Hint Video mode can help ensure that the green screen is removed accurately throughout the entire sequence.
Technical Specifications

CorridorKey 2 supports HDR and can export sequences in OpenEXR format with scene-linear color space. It processes videos at their native resolution and includes robust temporal stabilization via Hann windowing to eliminate edge flicker on masks. This means you get cleaner, more stable footage without the need for extensive manual adjustments.

For example, if your video has a lot of motion blur or out-of-focus areas, CorridorKey 2’s advanced features will help maintain clarity and stability in the final output. The tool also supports real-time processing, which can be particularly useful when working on live streams or during post-production editing sessions where quick adjustments are necessary.
Multi-Model Approach

One of the most significant improvements is CorridorKey 2’s multi-model approach. Instead of relying on a single neural network, it combines predictions from three base models: C-RADIOv4 by NVIDIA, MoGe-2 by Microsoft, and RVM by Google DeepMind. This combination enhances accuracy in challenging scenarios like occlusions, hair, fur, semi-transparent objects, out-of-focus areas, and blended backgrounds.

Imagine you’re working on a scene where the subject has long hair that moves with every frame. Traditional methods might struggle to accurately remove the green screen without leaving artifacts or cutting off parts of the hair. With CorridorKey 2’s multi-model approach, these issues are significantly reduced, ensuring smoother transitions and cleaner results.
System Requirements

To run CorridorKey 2, you need an RTX 30 series or newer GPU with at least 4 GB of VRAM for 720p footage and 6 GB for 1080p. The software is compatible with Windows and Linux systems, and the code is available on GitHub while weights are hosted on Hugging Face.

This means that if you’re working on a high-resolution video project, you’ll need to ensure your system meets these requirements to take full advantage of CorridorKey 2’s capabilities. For instance, if you're editing a 4K video with complex green screen removal needs, having the necessary hardware is crucial for optimal performance.
Plugins and Standalone Application

CorridorKey 2 comes with plugins for popular video editing tools like DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects + Premiere Pro, and Blender (Windows and Mac; Linux support in beta). There’s also a standalone application available for those who prefer to use the tool without integrating it into their existing workflow.

For instance, if you’re already deeply embedded in your current video editing software but want to try out CorridorKey 2, you can simply install the plugin and start using it right away. Alternatively, if you prefer working with a dedicated application, the standalone version offers all the same features without requiring any additional setup.
Commercial Use

The good news is that CorridorKey 2 can be used freely for commercial projects. This means you don’t have to worry about licensing fees or restrictions when using it on your professional work.

So, if you’re a video editor working on a client project and need to remove green screens quickly and efficiently, CorridorKey 2 provides the flexibility and freedom to do so without any additional costs. For example, if you're under tight deadlines for multiple projects, having access to this tool can significantly streamline your workflow.
What’s Stored?

CorridorKey 2 processes each frame of your input video and generates accurate predictions for removing the green screen. It stores these predictions as matte layers that can be exported in various formats like OpenEXR with scene-linear color space, ensuring high-quality output suitable for professional use.

However, it does not store any personal data or user-specific information beyond what is necessary to process your input video and generate the desired output. This ensures privacy and security while maintaining efficiency in workflow management.
What’s Excluded?

While CorridorKey 2 excels at removing green screens in complex scenes, there are still some limitations. For example, extremely challenging scenarios like highly reflective surfaces or very fine details might require additional manual adjustments. Additionally, while it supports HDR and OpenEXR export formats, other less common formats may not be supported.

So, if you’re working on a project that involves these specific challenges, you might need to supplement CorridorKey 2 with traditional methods or other specialized tools. For instance, if your video includes intricate patterns or textures that are difficult for AI to distinguish from the green screen, manual retouching may still be necessary.
User Controls

Users have control over the hint modes (No Hint, First-Frame Hint, Full-Hint Video) and can choose which model predictions they want to use. This flexibility allows for customization based on the specific needs of each project.

For instance, if you’re working on a scene with minimal movement, using the No Hint mode might be sufficient. However, if your subject is moving significantly throughout the video, opting for Full-Hint Video could provide better results. You can also fine-tune settings like edge detection and noise reduction to achieve optimal output quality.
Availability

CorridorKey 2 is available now and can be downloaded from GitHub. The code and weights are hosted on Hugging Face, making it accessible to developers and content creators alike. Plugins for various editing software are also available, with Linux support in beta.

So, if you’re ready to give CorridorKey 2 a try, you can start by downloading the standalone application or integrating one of the plugins into your existing workflow. For example, if you're using DaVinci Resolve for your video editing needs, installing the plugin will allow you to leverage CorridorKey 2’s capabilities directly within your preferred software.
What This Does Not Prove

While CorridorKey 2 is an impressive tool for green screen removal, it does not prove that AI will replace all traditional video editing techniques. It’s still important to have a solid understanding of chroma keying and other manual methods, especially when dealing with complex or unusual scenarios.

Moreover, while the multi-model approach enhances accuracy in many cases, there are still limitations and challenges where human expertise remains crucial. For instance, certain visual effects or intricate compositing tasks may require a blend of AI tools like CorridorKey 2 and traditional editing techniques to achieve the desired results.
Practical Takeaway

For video editors and content creators looking for an efficient way to handle green screen footage, CorridorKey 2 offers a powerful solution. Its advanced features and flexibility make it particularly useful for complex scenes that traditional methods struggle with. However, if you already have a workflow that meets your needs, there’s no rush to switch just yet.

So, are you ready to give CorridorKey 2 a try? Do you have other tools that work better for your specific needs? Let us know in the comments below!

text:
That evening, I found a folded note beneath my keyboard.

It was in Denise’s handwriting.

Dear Olivia,

Thank you for making me feel welcome in a place where I often felt invisible. Don’t stop asking questions, and don’t let anyone convince you that your work has no value.

Keep going.

I read it twice.

Then I noticed something unusual.

At the bottom of the note, Denise had written an address and a date.

The date was the following Friday.

Beside it were four words.

Please come if you can.

I had no idea what she was inviting me to.

But on Friday afternoon, I left work early and drove to the address.

It was a large conference center downtown.

Outside the entrance, a banner displayed the name of a national organization dedicated to improving access to medical technology.

And beneath the organization’s name was a photograph of Denise.

I stood frozen on the sidewalk.

Because the woman who had spent eleven years cleaning our offices was about to receive an award for something I never could have imagined.

I entered the conference center and followed the signs to the main auditorium.

Hundreds of people were seated inside. Some wore business suits, others wore hospital uniforms, and several had traveled from different states.

I found Denise sitting in the front row.

She wore a beautiful navy dress and a silver necklace.

When she saw me, she smiled and patted the empty seat beside her.

“You came!”

“Denise, what is this?”

She laughed softly.

“You’ll find out.”

The ceremony began with a presentation about a nonprofit organization that helped hospitals in underserved communities obtain affordable medical equipment.

The speaker explained that many hospitals discarded equipment that could still be used safely after proper inspection, refurbishment, and certification.

For years, the organization had worked with engineers, technicians, and medical professionals to redirect suitable equipment to clinics that needed it.

Then the speaker announced a special recognition award.

“This year’s recipient spent more than two decades working in medical equipment quality assurance. After leaving that profession to care for her husband, she continued volunteering her expertise to help hospitals improve safety procedures and prevent unnecessary equipment waste.”

My heart began pounding.

The speaker continued.

“She has helped train technicians, reviewed refurbishment procedures, and developed practical checklists that are now used by several participating facilities.”

Then he said Denise’s full name.

Denise Williams.

I turned toward her.

She was already standing.

The auditorium erupted in applause as she walked toward the stage.

I sat there, stunned.

The speaker explained that Denise had spent 24 years working as a quality assurance specialist for a medical equipment manufacturer before stepping away from her career to care for her husband after a serious illness.

After he died, she had needed steady employment that offered predictable hours, so she took a cleaning job through a facilities contractor.

She never stopped volunteering.

In her spare time, she reviewed equipment documentation, helped train volunteers, and supported hospitals that lacked experienced technical staff.

She had never told me any of this.

When Denise reached the microphone, she looked out at the audience.

“I’m grateful for this award,” she began. “But I want to say something about the people who work in jobs that others overlook.”

The room became quiet.

“Sometimes, when you wear a uniform, people assume that your entire life is contained inside that uniform. They see the work you do for them, but they don’t wonder what you know, what you’ve accomplished, or what you might still have to offer.”

She paused.

“I’ve met cleaners who were teachers, delivery drivers who were engineers, and cafeteria workers who once ran businesses of their own. People don’t stop being knowledgeable simply because their circumstances change.”

text:
Ethiopia: Landlocked by History, Portless By Choice 

Ethiopia has five neighbors with eight ports, yet it still complains about ports. 

The reason is not geography or logistics. 

It is that Addis Ababa does not want to lease a port. It wants to own one. Or two.

The distinction is not semantic. A lease is a commercial arrangement. Ownership, or the functional equivalent of it—a land corridor under Ethiopian administration plus a port sized for its navy—is a territorial claim dressed up as a logistics problem. 

That difference has driven the last several years of Ethiopian diplomacy and, more quietly, its choice of partners.

Here is how the demand for “sovereign sea access” has played out, port by port.

1. Port Sudan, Sudan

The internationally recognized government of Sudan controls Port Sudan. Ethiopia has instead positioned itself as a conduit for UAE arms shipments to the Rapid Support Forces, the main group trying to unseat that government.

Outcome: no deal.

2–3. Massawa and Assab, Eritrea

The 1993 Eritrea-Ethiopia port treaty gave Ethiopia preferential treatment precisely because, as the preamble stated, Ethiopia has “special needs as a landlocked state.” 

The terms were already more favorable than a standard commercial lease. Ethiopia rejected them. What it has sought instead is a land corridor inside Eritrea under its own administration and a port large enough for its navy.

Outcome: no deal.

4–6. Doraleh, Tadjourah, Damerjog — Djibouti

Ethiopia already moves the overwhelming majority of its trade through Doraleh. When it asked for access to Tadjourah, Djibouti was prepared to negotiate until the actual requirement became clear: a land corridor under Ethiopian administration and a port sized for naval use.

Outcome: no deal. 

7–8. Berbera and Bosaso, Somalia

On 1 January 2024 Ethiopia signed an agreement for the use of Berbera on terms it preferred. 

But the arrangement was not binding: it was concluded with an entity that lacked the legal authority to enter into it. 

Before the year ended, Ethiopia signed a second agreement acknowledging Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, effectively walking back the earlier one.

Outcome: reversed.

9–10. Mombasa and Lamu, Kenya

Lamu was meant to serve Ethiopia and South Sudan under the LAPSSET framework, complete with railways and the diversion of South Sudanese oil. 

Cost realities have left the project barely built since 2012. Lamu is used, modestly, for southern Ethiopian industry—by road, not rail. 

The Mombasa–Moyale route exists and is barely used.

Outcome: marginal.

The pattern is consistent. Where a commercial lease or transit arrangement is on offer, Ethiopia has either declined or redefined the request until the other party walks away. 

Where a partner is willing to overlook sovereignty questions, the arrangement has not survived contact with international law or regional pressure. 

The demand for “sovereign sea access” has not produced a port. It has produced a series of rejected or reversed arrangements and a region that has grown more wary of the ask.

Ethiopia has claimed it has a “natural” right to the Sea.  Nations don’t have natural right. 

Ethiopia has claimed that it has historical right to the Sea.  But the net history of Ethiopia is that of a landlocked nation, except when the Cold War calcifications dictated it be given someone else’s Sea, reversed and internationally recognized. 

Ethiopia has also claimed it had legal right to sovereign access to Sea.  It hasn’t even tried to argue that coherently since it had signed multiple agreements recognizing its borders with Eritrea make her landlocked. 

Ethiopia is historically landlocked but powerless by choice.

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the afternoon of October 23, 1973, in a federal courtroom in Washington, the long and bitter contest over the White House tapes came to a sudden and unexpected end. Charles Alan Wright, the Texas law professor who had carried the President’s defense through months of litigation, stood before Judge John J. Sirica and announced that Richard Nixon would comply in all respects with the court’s order. The subpoenaed recordings would be turned over.

It had not always seemed so. Sixteen months earlier, on a June night in 1972, five men were arrested inside the Democratic National Committee offices in the Watergate complex. What began as a bungled burglary slowly revealed a larger cover-up. Through the spring and summer of 1973 the Senate Watergate Committee heard testimony that drew the public closer to the truth. Then, on July 16, Alexander Butterfield disclosed that President Nixon had ordered a voice-activated system installed to record conversations in the Oval Office, the Cabinet Room, and elsewhere. From that moment the tapes themselves became the central prize of the investigation.

Special Prosecutor Archibald Cox moved at once to obtain nine of the recordings. Judge Sirica, a tough jurist with little patience for claims of absolute executive privilege, ordered the tapes delivered for private review. The Court of Appeals affirmed. For three months the White House resisted, insisting that the confidentiality of presidential conversations was essential and that no court could compel their surrender.

On October 19 Nixon offered a compromise: Senator John C. Stennis would listen to the tapes and verify a White House summary. Cox refused. The next day came the Saturday Night Massacre. Nixon ordered Attorney General Elliot Richardson to dismiss the special prosecutor. Richardson, bound by the assurances he had given the Senate, refused and resigned. Deputy Attorney General William Ruckelshaus likewise refused and was dismissed. Solicitor General Robert Bork carried out the order. The special prosecutor’s office was sealed. Within hours the country learned of the cascade of resignations and the firing.

The reaction was swift. Tens of thousands of telegrams poured into Washington. Members of Congress from both parties spoke of impeachment. In the space of a single weekend the constitutional crisis that had been gathering for months appeared to reach its breaking point.

Then, on the afternoon of the 23rd, the reversal came. Wright told Sirica that the President, faced with the certainty of a contempt citation and the growing likelihood of impeachment, had decided to obey the court. The tapes would be indexed and submitted. Sirica broke into a smile and said he was very happy that the President had reached the decision. The crisis that had flared so brightly only days earlier seemed, for the moment, to recede.

It was not the end. Gaps would later be discovered on the recordings. Further subpoenas would be issued. The Supreme Court would ultimately speak in July 1974. And the tape of a June 23, 1972 conversation—the so-called smoking gun—would leave Nixon no choice but resignation. Yet on that October afternoon the President of the United States, after months of defiance, yielded to a federal judge. In a republic founded on the principle that no one stands above the law, the moment carried a weight that few who lived through it would forget.

In a small industrial town in Ohio, three childhood friends—Marcus, Elena, and Sam—gathered every Friday evening at a local diner. Over cheap coffee and slices of pie, they shared the rhythm of their lives, bound by years of history and shared dreams.

Yet, outside the diner’s warm windows, the national economic landscape was quietly shifting. Marcus felt the weight of inflation in his grocery bill, Elena navigated the unpredictable gig economy to launch a small business, and Sam watched tech advances redefine his manufacturing job. The American dream didn't feel broken to them, but it certainly felt transformed.

Despite the fluctuating markets and shifting times, their weekly table remained fixed. They lent each other money during tight months, celebrated small victories, and offered steady advice when uncertainty loomed. Their story was uniquely American: while the economy dictated the cost of living, it was their steadfast friendship that gave life its true value.

Gold vs Oil: A 44% Plunge No Dollar Price Can Show

The price of gold expressed in barrels of oil offers a different perspective than its dollar price, revealing a significant loss in purchasing power over the past year.

On October 20, 2026, at a gold price of $4,125.07 per ounce, one ounce could buy about 38 barrels of Brent crude oil, down from about 67 barrels a year earlier, when gold traded at $4,115 per ounce and Brent cost about $61 per barrel.

This decline is purely arithmetic: oil prices rose by approximately 78%, while gold barely changed, resulting in an ounce losing about 44% of its purchasing power in terms of oil. The ratio remains approximately twice its long-term median, even after accounting for the oil spike.

According to Eco3min Research, the monthly average since 1986 is about 18.5 barrels per ounce, with the high figure attributed to rising gold prices, not falling oil prices.

@GoldSilver gives an average of approximately 15 to 20 for the period since 1970, a difference explained by the use of WTI (West Texas Intermediate) crude oil rather than Brent. @eco3min  emphasized that this ratio has no automatic reversion level, so being twice the average is a fact, not a forecast.

The calculation depends on two prices: a $10 change in Brent changes the figure by approximately 3-4 barrels, while a $100 change in gold changes it by about 1 barrel. To reach the median of 18.5, Brent would need to be about $223 per barrel at the current gold price, or gold would need to fall to about $2,010 at the current Brent price, arithmetic calculations, not forecasts.

Markets await the US Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee meeting scheduled for October 27 and 28, which will affect the dollar price of gold. Gold can fall when oil spikes because rising oil prices intensify inflation concerns, increase the likelihood of higher interest rates, and push up real yields, making holding a non-income-generating metal more costly. @Reuters  reported on October 21 that precious metal prices fell on such concerns.

This dynamic says little about an ounce's purchasing power, which is what matters for investors, especially those whose expenses depend on energy prices.

A @MorganStanley  study dated May 5, 2026, found gold fell 14.5% in March following the start of the Iran conflict, suggesting the energy crisis reduced gold's effectiveness as a hedge.

Ultimately, the gold-in-oil ratio shows purchasing power, not just screen value, and a central bank raising rates will not increase oil supply if Persian Gulf deliveries are disrupted. text:
The Top 5 Travel Destinations for Nature Immersion

For travelers seeking a deeper connection with the natural world, some destinations offer far more than beautiful scenery. They provide opportunities to witness wildlife in its natural habitat, explore remote landscapes, experience unique ecosystems, and gain a greater appreciation for the planet's biodiversity. The following five destinations represent some of the finest nature-focused experiences on Earth, ranging from polar wilderness to tropical rainforest.

1. Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
Hallmark Feature

Extraordinary wildlife found nowhere else on Earth, much of which shows little fear of humans due to centuries of isolation.

Best Things to Do
Snorkel alongside sea lions, marine iguanas, and sea turtles
Observe blue-footed boobies and giant tortoises
Visit multiple islands to experience distinct ecosystems
Kayak through volcanic coastlines
Hike lava fields and volcanic terrain
Participate in naturalist-led wildlife excursions
Best Time to Visit
December to May: Warmer waters and calmer seas
June to November: Excellent wildlife activity and nutrient-rich waters for marine life
Ideal Length of Stay

7-10 days

Best Travel Modality

Expedition cruise

A small-ship expedition cruise provides access to remote islands that cannot be reached independently and allows visitors to experience the archipelago as Charles Darwin once did.

Physical Activity Level

Moderate

Activities often include:

Wet beach landings
Uneven volcanic trails
Snorkeling
Zodiac boat transfers
Mobility Considerations

Travelers with limited mobility may face challenges due to:

Rocky shore landings
Limited accessibility infrastructure
Small expedition vessels

Some cruise operators offer more accessible programs, but travelers requiring significant mobility assistance should carefully evaluate options before booking.

2. Antarctica
Hallmark Feature

The world's most pristine wilderness, featuring immense icebergs, glaciers, and vast penguin colonies.

Best Things to Do
Observe emperor, Adélie, and gentoo penguins
Cruise among towering ice formations
Spot whales, seals, and seabirds
Participate in guided shore landings
Take Zodiac excursions through icy channels
Experience the silence and scale of Earth's last great wilderness
Best Time to Visit
November through March
Peak wildlife viewing generally occurs from January to February
Ideal Length of Stay

10-14 days

Best Travel Modality

Expedition cruise

The vast majority of visitors reach Antarctica aboard specialized expedition vessels departing from Argentina or Chile.

Physical Activity Level

Moderate to High

Activities can include:

Walking on snow and ice
Boarding Zodiacs
Climbing slippery gangways
Optional kayaking and polar camping
Mobility Considerations

Travelers with limited mobility should carefully reconsider this destination.

Challenges include:

Unpredictable weather
Moving vessels
Zodiac embarkation
Uneven terrain
Lack of accessibility infrastructure

While some operators accommodate certain limitations, Antarctica remains one of the least accessible destinations in the world.

3. Namibia
Hallmark Feature

One of the most dramatic desert ecosystems on Earth, where giant sand dunes meet wildlife-rich landscapes.

Best Things to Do
Watch sunrise over the towering dunes of Sossusvlei
Visit Deadvlei's ancient petrified landscape
Track desert-adapted elephants
Explore Etosha National Park
Observe star-filled skies in one of the world's darkest environments
Visit the Skeleton Coast
Best Time to Visit
May through October
Dry season provides outstanding wildlife viewing
Ideal Length of Stay

10-14 days

Best Travel Modality

Motorized overland safari and air touring

A combination of luxury 4x4 vehicles and regional flights allows access to Namibia's vast and remote regions.

Physical Activity Level

Low to Moderate

Most activities involve:

Vehicle-based game viewing
Short nature walks
Optional dune climbing
Mobility Considerations

Namibia is among the more accessible wilderness destinations.

Travelers with limited mobility can enjoy:

Vehicle safaris
Scenic drives
Many luxury lodges

However, climbing dunes such as Big Daddy at Sossusvlei requires significant exertion and may not be suitable.

4. Costa Rica
Hallmark Feature

The world's most accessible tropical biodiversity hotspot, containing approximately 5% of Earth's biodiversity within a relatively small country.

Best Things to Do
Explore the cloud forests of Monteverde
Search for sloths, monkeys, and toucans
Walk suspension bridges through the rainforest canopy
Visit Arenal Volcano
Whitewater raft jungle rivers
Experience turtle nesting along the Caribbean coast
Relax in natural hot springs
Best Time to Visit
December through April (dry season)
May through July offers fewer crowds and lush landscapes
Ideal Length of Stay

8-12 days

Best Travel Modality

Land-based touring with motorized transportation

Well-developed roads and domestic flights make Costa Rica easy to explore.

Physical Activity Level

Low to High (customizable)

Options range from:

Easy wildlife viewing
Gentle nature walks
Challenging rainforest hikes
Adventure sports
Mobility Considerations

Costa Rica is increasingly accommodating to travelers with mobility limitations.

Many:

National parks
Wildlife centers
Lodges
Guided excursions

offer accessible options. Travelers can tailor activities according to their abilities.

5. Alaska
Hallmark Feature

A vast wilderness of glaciers, mountains, fjords, forests, and abundant wildlife spread across a landscape larger than many countries.

Best Things to Do
Cruise through Glacier Bay
Watch bears fishing for salmon
Observe humpback whales and orcas
Ride the Alaska Railroad
Explore Denali National Park
Take flightseeing tours over glaciers
Experience Native Alaskan culture
Best Time to Visit
June through August for the best weather
September for autumn colors and fewer crowds
Ideal Length of Stay

7-14 days

Best Travel Modality

Combination of ocean cruise, rail travel, and motorcoach touring

Alaska offers one of the most varied transportation experiences in North America.

Physical Activity Level

Low to Moderate

Most wildlife and scenery can be enjoyed through:

Cruise excursions
Rail journeys
Scenic drives

Optional hikes can range from easy to strenuous.

Mobility Considerations

Alaska is one of the most accessible nature destinations.

Many major:

Cruise ships
Visitor centers
Rail services
Wildlife cruises

are accessible to travelers with mobility limitations.

Comparison at a Glance
Destination Hallmark Feature Best Modality Activity Level Mobility Friendly? Ideal StayGalápagos Islands Unique endemic wildlife Expedition Cruise Moderate Limited 7-10 days
Antarctica Polar wilderness and ice landscapes Expedition Cruise Moderate-High Not Recommended 10-14 days
Namibia Desert ecosystems and wildlife Overland Safari Low-Moderate Generally Good 10-14 days
Costa Rica Tropical biodiversity Land Touring Flexible Good 8-12 days
Alaska Glaciers and wildlife Cruise/Rail/Land Low-Moderate Excellent 7-14 days
Final Thoughts

If your goal is the greatest wildlife encounter, the Galápagos Islands are difficult to surpass. For travelers seeking the planet's most remote wilderness, Antarctica offers an experience unlike any other. Namibia delivers dramatic landscapes and safari adventures with relatively little physical demand, while Costa Rica combines accessibility with astonishing biodiversity. For travelers who want magnificent scenery with the least physical challenge, Alaska provides perhaps the most comfortable pathway into the natural world.

Among these five destinations, Alaska and Costa Rica are generally the best choices for travelers with limited mobility, while Antarctica requires the greatest physical adaptability and poses the most significant accessibility challenges.

Texas Has the Oil. America Needs the Fuel. So Why Are We Still Paying So Much at the Pump?

15 Questions that Address Reasons

America is sitting on enormous oil reserves, Texas is pumping millions of barrels a day, and the United States is producing more crude oil than any other country, yet Americans are still paying prices at the pump that make everyday life harder. 

The public is told that global markets, refinery costs, foreign conflicts and taxes explain the bill, and those factors are real, but they do not excuse the need for accountability. Energy companies operate to maximize profits, not to guarantee affordable fuel for American families, and when overseas buyers offer competitive prices, domestic consumers do not automatically get priority.

 Meanwhile, politicians promise energy independence without always explaining why producing more oil does not translate into cheaper gasoline. The hard truth is that having the oil is not the same as controlling the price, and $1 gasoline is not a realistic promise without extraordinary conditions, major cost reductions or government subsidies. 

But Americans have every right to demand transparency about refinery margins, taxes, export policies, competition and the decisions that shape what they pay. 

If America has the resources, infrastructure and production capacity to be an energy powerhouse, then the public deserves a serious explanation of why that advantage does not deliver more affordable fuel, and which policies would actually make a difference.

"Democrats who favor Medicare for All have given Republicans a huge opportunity.

Far from hiding from the healthcare debate, Republicans should be piling on and forcing Democrats to defend their crazy idea of a Washington-run national healthcare system. Republicans should also offer a positive alternative.

There are three major reasons to reject Medicare for All.

First, Sen. Bernie Sanders’ Medicare for All bill could force American taxpayers to pay for healthcare for illegal immigrants. The bill makes residency, not citizenship, the basis for coverage and contains no explicit exclusion for people here illegally. Sanders himself has said they would be covered.

An April 2025 poll by America’s New Majority Project found that 62 percent of voters opposed states using taxpayer money to provide Medicaid benefits for illegal immigrants, with 43 percent strongly opposed. Another 62 percent favored a federal law prohibiting it. Three out of four Americans supported stronger identity verification for Medicaid applicants, compared with just 18 percent opposed.

The questions were about Medicaid, not Medicare for All, but they reveal strong opposition to taxpayer-funded coverage for illegal immigrants.

As inarticulate as the GOP often is, Republicans should be able to win 75 percent-to-18 percent debates.

Second, Medicare for All would create an enormous new Washington healthcare bureaucracy. This is not speculation. Under Sanders’ bill, Washington would determine hospital budgets, set doctors’ fees, decide which drugs are covered, and prohibit private insurance that duplicates government coverage.

There are serious problems with today’s insurance companies. They deny claims, restrict networks, and bury doctors in paperwork. But the answer to private-sector bureaucracy is not an even bigger government bureaucracy.

Under Medicare for All, hospital budgets are described as “negotiated.” But when Washington writes the rules and controls nearly all the money, what kind of negotiation is that?

That is not simply government paying the bills. It is government controlling healthcare.

Third, guaranteeing health insurance is not the same as guaranteeing healthcare.

Congress can pass a law guaranteeing every American healthcare. It cannot pass a law creating more doctors, hospital beds, or available appointments."

text:
🇦🇱| Day 145: An Empty Chair, a Pillow, and a Sheet of Paper Labeled "Dialogue"

October 23, 2026. Tirana, Albania. Day 145 of the "Flamingo Revolution."

Rama placed a chair completed with a pillow outside the Prime Minister’s office, set down a sheet of paper marked "DIALOGUE," and positioned a camera to capture it.

There was no one in the frame. No students. No professors. No one to engage in dialogue.

There was only a man too afraid to face a real conversation, and a chair waiting for a guest who did not exist.

💥 What have the students received over these 145 days?

Water cannons. Tear gas. Stun grenades. Batons.

6,800 people have been arrested, most of them minors. A 15-year-old boy lost a hand. A 14-year-old lost his teeth. A 16-year-old lost an eye.

And yet, he set out a chair with a pillow, calling it "dialogue."

A pillow is meant to provide comfort to the person sitting on it. He offered comfort to an empty chair while the actual students were met with stun grenades.

🎯 Why an empty chair?

Because the real students rejected him. They overturned the chair. They tore up the paper labeled "Dialogue."

The next day, he replaced it with a concrete block. The students rejected that, too.

A Prime Minister rejected three times by his own people.his fourth gesture was not one of sincerity, but a staged scene for a photograph. He wasn't seeking dialogue; he was crafting an image to be captured and sent to Brussels and Washington: "I am trying, but they refuse to show up."

📜 What else has he done during these 145 days?

In the same week he set out that empty chair, he announced in the dead of night.that the government might lower the age of criminal responsibility, effectively clearing the way to imprison the children who were protesting.

That same year, armored vehicles sourced from Türkiye and Israel appeared on the streets of Tirana.  That same year, he looked into the camera and said: "You are incompetent. You are envious. Your day of reckoning has arrived."

Then, he set out a chair completed with a cushion.

In his vocabulary, the word "dialogue" much like "Europe," "reform," or "democracy".is merely decorative. It looks good in a photograph, but it has no existence in reality.

⚔️ Why the students refuse to sit down

A student leader put it clearly: "A true student will not sit in that chair."

To sit down would be to accept a premise that this dialogue is sincere.which is, in fact, false.

What does a genuine dialogue require? It requires acknowledging that the other side has demands, and the right to voice them. It requires putting down the truncheons and opening the doors.

What did he set aside? Nothing at all. He opened a door revealing only an empty chair.

Someone who responds to a leaking classroom ceiling with stun grenades has no business using a chair to invite dialogue. Someone who meets student protests with armored vehicles has no business using a cushion to feign sincerity.

🔻 Day 145

Day 145. An empty chair. A cushion. A sheet of paper. A man who, having been rejected three times, continues his performance.

The real students are not in that chair. They are in the streets, in detention centers, in hospitals holding their ground, having not retreated a single step for the past 145 days.

They have no need for his cushion. They need him to leave.

And so, he sits in his office, speaking into the camera to an empty chair. Because that is the only thing left that is still willing to listen to him.

Long live the students of Albania. Long live the Flamingo Revolution on its 145th day. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

As I read it through Khan's Exhaustion Asymmetry (KEA), this is what exhaustion sounds like on the stronger side. When a war starts being measured in fuel prices and election dates, the people at home are no longer asking how to win, but how long this can go on.
Iran, on the other hand, has been badly hurt but it is still standing. It knows it cannot match American power, so it makes every round more expensive, besides passing part of the bill to the world economy, and that is a cost Washington cannot ignore for long.
At the same time, the door to talks has not closed. Araghchi says the negotiating table is still there, Pakistan and Qatar continue to carry messages between the two sides, and even Rubio has thanked Doha for its efforts.
I have always believed that wars like this are rarely won. They end when someone can offer both sides a way out that does not look like surrender. The question is whether that way out will be found before the next escalation decides for everyone.

The Art of the Deal: Jared Kushner’s Hacked Phone Revealed His Secret Negotiations—Including More Than $700 Million in Transfers
An exclusive excerpt from Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East examines how bank accounts linked the president’s son-in-law—and former senior adviser—to Israel, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia.
By Matthew Cole
October 22, 2026

In late spring 2020, a source I knew to be reliable called me with a story. The Dutch government had hacked into Jared Kushner’s phone and monitored him as he accessed a Dubai-based bank account. What was odd, the source said, was that the money in the account—hundreds of millions of dollars—had come from a bank in Azerbaijan. Most importantly, Kushner appeared to have transferred significant amounts of money from the Dubai account to other individuals, including a warlord, a mercenary and a one-time hit man. The story sounded preposterous, I told my source. And yet.

Six months later, I found myself speaking with someone else about the UAE government and their use of mercenaries in conflicts around the Middle East and Africa when I asked, on a whim, whether they knew anything about Kushner and bank transfers from a UAE account. My acquaintance grew quiet. Then they replied, “Yes.”

Over the next four years, I came to learn that, sometime in late 2017, the Netherlands Defense Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) made a startling discovery. A General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU) operative, a dark web hacker specializing in stolen bank data, was traveling to the UK for an espionage mission. They reached out to the British government for permission to apprehend him when he arrived. The British agreed.

When the Russian national arrived in England, the Dutch informed him that he had two options: he could work for them against the GRU, or the British would arrest him. Once in UK government custody, the operative would be charged with espionage. If convicted, he would spend years in a British prison. The Russian chose to change his employer.

Later that year, the Russian operative gave the Dutch spies access to one of the GRU’s most sensitive assets. Located in Rostov, Russia, the GRU’s hacking and cyber team operated a remote server on which they stored some of their bounty. During their search through these secret files, the Dutch found something astonishing: screenshots of Jared Kushner’s iPhone.

In The Hague, the MIVD hacking team tried to reverse engineer the Russian penetration of Kushner’s iPhone. Kushner owned what was then the latest model, the iPhone X. Released in November 2017, it featured Face ID, a state-of-the-art security feature that Apple had promoted at its launch. The Dutch team had been trying to pick the phone’s door lock, so to speak, when it occurred to them that the Russians may have found an unlocked window to gain entry instead. Their hypothesis was correct. By early 2018, the MIVD had found a vulnerability in the iPhone that gave them access. The security exploit wasn’t perfect, however. Some malware allows a hacker to turn a victim’s phone into a microphone and video camera, turn the phone on or off, and pull and add files. The Dutch solution did not provide that level of access. Instead, when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner’s screen as he used it, filing their own cache of surveillance on their internal computer servers.

As they monitored Kushner’s phone, they discovered he used it to log in to a UAE bank account. By the time the Dutch spies had visibility into the phone, the account had received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan. Their initial assessment was that the bank account was affiliated with the government there.

“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source who knew of the UAE’s deal with Kushner said.
For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence mystery to unravel. Nearly everything they worked on had a tinge of Russian conspiracy. A little over a year into Trump’s first presidency, the MIVD, like FBI agents and federal prosecutors in Washington working on the Robert Mueller investigation, had only part of the story.

Kushner, UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed (MBZ) and Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) of Saudi Arabia, converged at an auspicious moment. MBS wanted to be crown prince. MBZ wanted to blow up Obama’s Iran nuclear deal, and Kushner wanted both to help him force the Palestinians into a deal that Israel would accept. Despite the perception of his wealth, Kushner was not entirely financially independent of his parents, and the family business, Kushner Companies, faced a billion-dollar loan coming due on their trophy property, the Manhattan office building at 666 Fifth Avenue.

Early in the first Trump administration, MBZ and MBS offered to pay for a slush fund dedicated to helping the new administration with foreign policy goals. The idea was to help pay for Trump’s promised wall between Mexico and the US, for example, in an effort to secure a second term in the White House. The two Arab royals initially discussed with Kushner putting more than $10 billion into the effort. Within months, though, as MBZ pushed the Trump administration to help back MBS’s effort to become his country’s crown prince—and future king—the broader foreign policy slush fund idea fizzled. Instead, MBZ and MBS initially, and then MBZ alone, put at least $2 billion into at least two bank accounts for Kushner. It is unclear how the royals organized their $2 billion in combined payments, but they effectively split the cost. For the purposes of explanation, it is best to understand where and how each bank account was controlled.

“The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.”
Bank account Alpha was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, the largest in the UAE, and was overseen by MBZ’s brother, Tahnoon bin Zayed, who served as the bank’s chairman. Beginning in 2017, the Saudis and Emiratis transferred roughly $750 million into the Alpha account. Alpha would be used as a foreign policy fund. This money would be overseen and partially managed by Kushner and MBZ, who, in their effort to strike a grand bargain to end the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, believed the region’s map needed to be redrawn.

“Jared was looking for shortcuts in his diplomacy,” a source who knew of the UAE’s deal with Kushner said. This person held discussions with both senior UAE and Israeli officials about the secret financial arrangement between Kushner, the UAE, and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia. “Jared promised MBZ that he’d push their agenda with Trump if they participated in a fund. He wanted normalization with Israel so that business could take off.” A slush fund—a shared pool of money for off-the-books diplomatic objectives—was a common form of Gulf Arab government corruption, this person explained. “The Emiratis and the Saudis do this once a year. A billion or two is nothing for them, and if it gets them what they want, it’s money well spent.”

The Alpha account looked like the funding source of a UAE government program, by which MBZ paid his bureaucrats their salaries or funded government-run schools. But how and through whom the money flowed into the Alpha account revealed that it was intended to remain secret, more akin to a covert and illicit scheme, given that it was managed in part by a senior advisor to the president of the United States.

The Dutch spies who monitored the Alpha account noted that all of it was sent by a bank in Azerbaijan in American dollars. Azerbaijan plays a unique role in money laundering. Its central bank maintains high levels of US dollars in its reserves but does not adhere to the highest standards of bank transparency. As a result, Azerbaijani banks have well-established but unadvertised practices of serving as way stations for large transfers, in which a foreign currency is exchanged for an equal amount in dollars. For a roughly 6 to 7 percent fee on the transaction, some Azerbaijani banks will accept a transfer from a client who wishes to move Saudi riyals or Emirati dirhams totaling hundreds of millions of dollars. The Saudi or Emirati client sends the money to the Azerbaijani bank, which then uses a different internal bank account to transfer the equivalent US dollars to the client’s requested destination. For auditors, this shadow trade can’t be discerned.

A shallow audit, as the Dutch tried while monitoring Kushner’s iPhone, revealed nothing more than what appeared to be an Azerbaijani government–linked bank account that sent hundreds of millions of dollars to an account in Dubai. But there was another aspect of the Alpha account that the Dutch couldn’t see or understand, one that helped reveal the secret purpose of the money. Kushner did not own the bank account at First Abu Dhabi Bank. He was a signatory for an account managed and owned by an Emirati charity.

When MBZ and MBS first began contributing to the Alpha account in 2017, the Watani Al Emarat Foundation, a UAE government-funded charity, was run by Dherar Belhoul Al Falasi. Al Falasi was a technocrat and a member of the Federal National Council, and friends with one of MBZ’s closest friends and advisors. As a result, Al Falasi and the Watani Foundation had a second mission. The charity was used as a cover to move money in support of the country’s secret military and intelligence operations overseas. Under the Watani cover, Al Falasi helped facilitate the UAE’s secret weapons-purchasing programs, one confidential source who had direct knowledge of the charity’s proliferation program revealed. This source said that the Emiratis believed that the program’s status as a charity made its international transactions less likely to be scrutinized and therefore served as a useful cover for funding MBZ and his brother’s secret wars.

MBZ and Tahnoon made Kushner a signatory on the Alpha account with Watani. As a signatory, Jared had access to it and could, in theory, make transactions, but it technically wasn’t his account. One way to view what Kushner did with the Alpha account is to imagine him as the director of the CIA. Had he been running the government entity that managed and ran secret foreign programs, maintaining the account, again, with presidential approval and congressional disclosure, Kushner’s conduct would have been within his job’s responsibilities. But he was not the director of the CIA, whose position is approved by the Senate and whose operations are overseen and accountable to Congress. Instead, Kushner was overseen only by his father-in-law, who, according to four senior Trump administration officials—two national security advisors, a White House chief of staff, and a former CIA director—were unaware of any presidential authorization for Kushner to access a foreign government bank account. (Kushner’s counsel, however, said Kushner did not make any agreements or arrangements with leaders or officials in foreign countries that were not agreed to by the President of the United States and in the best interests of the United States.)

Regardless of whether he was a signatory or the owner, Jared was required by federal government regulations and the Internal Revenue Service to disclose his access to the account. Unless disclosed to and approved by the US government and reported on his tax returns, Kushner’s access to the Alpha account may have violated US law. (A lawyer for Mr. Kushner denied that his client had any knowledge of or connection to Al Falasi, the Watani charity, or a UAE bank account and stated that he had complied with all legal requirements when dealing with foreign governments.)

In addition to the Alpha bank account, MBZ put money into at least one other account intended for Kushner. By the spring of 2018, the crown prince had moved roughly $1 billion to Israel via Azerbaijan for Kushner. We will refer to this account as the Beta bank account. It is unclear how Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu first learned of MBZ’s money for Kushner, but a person briefed on the Beta account told me that the prime minister encouraged Kushner to have the money deposited in the Israeli Central Bank, in what would appear to be a government account. It is also unclear how Kushner used the money the UAE deposited into the Beta account for him, but according to the person with knowledge of the money, its allocation was for Kushner’s personal benefit. But as with the Alpha account, there were clues in the way the Beta account was managed.

Image may contain Donald Trump Jared Kushner Didier Burkhalter Adult Person People Head Face and Clothing
President Donald Trump with Jared Kushner and Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in 2017. GPO/Getty Images

Israel’s Central Bank does not operate personal accounts. The bank holds and transfers only government funds. The government accounts use a dual-key system, which requires two authorized individuals to make any transfers from the account as an oversight mechanism. Netanyahu required Kushner to inform him before making any transactions from the Beta account.

To do so, Kushner passed his messages through Ambassador David M. Friedman, who frequently met with Netanyahu. With the money in the Central Bank, it would be difficult, if not impossible, to connect MBZ’s payment to Jared. It is unclear if spies in the Netherlands had any indication of the Beta account. (Ambassador Friedman denied that he had any knowledge of, or involvement with, any UAE money made available to Kushner, or that he passed messages on Kushner’s behalf. “I know absolutely nothing about any of these allegations,” Friedman said, “and the specific allegations about me or my alleged involvement in this alleged scheme are 100% false.” Kushner’s counsel also said Kushner “has no idea” about any such account, and insisted that “there are no accounts and never were.”)

Apparently, Kushner faced the challenge of moving money from the Beta account in Israel to other accounts where he could have untraceable access to the funds. One person who worked with Kushner to move the money out of Israel said that much of it went to bank accounts in Cyprus before being moved elsewhere.

During Kushner’s secret financial arrangement with MBZ, he helped negotiate a third, altogether distinct account. As part of what was, at the time, a secret warming of diplomatic relations between Israel and the UAE, Kushner helped negotiate an agreement by Israel to help defend the UAE from a major Iranian military attack. The UAE needed to cover the cost of the emergency defense, however, and the government secretly made another transfer to Israel’s Central Bank. This was something like a rainy-day defense fund. Combined, the three accounts represented a secret foreign policy negotiated by Kushner with the leaders of Israel, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

Although Kushner’s position as senior advisor to the president was unpaid, he was an official government employee. Not only did his position require financial disclosures for ethics regulations, but each year he worked in the White House, he had to file both a public and confidential financial form, known as the Executive Branch Personnel Public Financial Disclosure Report, also known as a 278e disclosure. Because he had access to classified government secrets, Kushner was required to disclose any bank account to which he had signatory—or beneficiary—access.

Kushner’s apparent betrayal of the public trust, however, went further than his failure to disclose the secret Alpha account in the UAE or the Beta account in Israel. By giving him access to roughly $2 billion, regardless of how the money was used, MBZ and MBS were paying for his influence within the US government. Any efforts he made to shape US policy that came from a foreign government that had provided him with money would make him an agent of a foreign power. US law requires citizens who lobby on behalf of a foreign power to declare themselves and the country they are working on behalf of to the Justice Department.

One former prosecutor who worked on the Mueller investigation said that if Kushner promised anything to MBZ and MBS in return for the money they offered him—even if it was just speaking to his father-in-law—he may have violated federal bribery laws, as well as the foreign agent statute. (Mr. Kushner’s lawyer denied that Kushner violated any laws while serving in the White House.)

Steiner offers a specific path of the soul to clairvoyance ranging from inner preparation to direct encounter with higher spiritual realities.

A useful overview of the soul's journey to clairvoyance can be found in Steiner's How is Knowledge of the Higher Worlds Attained.
There, in a first chapter a kind of basic preparation of the soul is laid out called, namely:

- Conditions & Prerequisites, namely: 
- The Path of Veneration / Devotion (Ehrfurcht)
- Inner Life and Tranquility (Innere Ruhe)

The second chapter Stages of Initiation (Die Stufen der Einweihung) deals with the development of spiritual senses through preparatory exercises such as the focused observation of growth, decay, and life forces.

Now why this first chapter of soul preparation "through the Path of Veneration / Devotion and the cultivation of Inner Life and Tranquility"?

If indeed we stepped immediately to the focused observation of growth, decay, and life forces without the inner preparation mentioned in Chapter one, we might stumble on such questions as to: 

Where is this sensation supposed to arise when contemplating processes of decay on the one hand, and of growth on the other?
Is it perhaps in the abdomen, or in the heart region, or in some other "sphere'.

This first short preparatory chapter deals then with the Cultivation of the Inner Life, so as to make visible where indeed such sensations occur, or are to occur.
Namely, certain simple "exercises" are mentioned, so as to actually start noticing the inner world at all, for those who haven't yet brought it into focus.

And while this is simple, it has also a certain complexity.

Two things stand out in this Preparation or Cultivation of the soul life:

Inner calm and Veneration or Devotion.

- Inner calm, so as to simply, in that state of inner calm, observe the inner life and what unfolds and appears within it, as something coming from a spiritual realm.
Thus not to fight this life of the soul, to attain a state of inner peace perhaps, but in inner peace to notice the soul life itself as it is.

-Devotion, towards the life of the soul, it is to say by producing a feeling of veneration for what flows in and through the soul as a manifestation of something higher. 
This devotion needs to and can be produced by the soul.

By focusing thus on the life of the soul or inner life, the awareness of having an inner life or life of the soul can come about and sink in, for those who are not already aware of this soul-life.

While sensations and feelings are often associated with the body, and with bodily regions, to notice such an inner life—which is actually independent of the body—is then a first step. 
This life of the soul can also be called the field of my awareness, and does or can include the body, yet it is not restricted to the body, it is larger than the body. 
And it is not only independent of the body, it is also independent of space and time. 

To notice that we have a soul, and a soul life, is then a very first step to start situating subsequent exercises.

Chinese AI Model Offers Catalyst for Zimbabwe's Digitalisation Agenda

By Mairosi Watungwa - Ningxia, China

It was an eye-opening masterclass in media modernization. Yesterday, Heads of Journalists Organizations and Gen Z Media Youth Leaders from Belt and Road Countries toured the Ningxia Radio and Television Station (NRTV), witnessing a state-of-the-art broadcasting ecosystem that seamlessly fuses cutting-edge technology, creative industry synergy and Artificial Intelligence (AI).

From the expansive newsrooms to its multi-functional studios, NRTV stands as a paragon of integrated media infrastructure. The facilities are equipped with next-generation 4K/8K ultra-high-definition systems, virtual reality production suites and intelligent broadcast control technologies. What is most striking is its dual-purpose model: beyond news production, the studios serve as a thriving hub for the wider creative economy. According to NRTV Director Ms Zhang Rang, to date more than 100 films and productions from external organizations have been shot utilizing NRTVs facilities, dramatically lowering filming production costs and turnaround times. It is a scalable, commercially viable studio model from which Zimbabwe can take a decisive leaf.

Zimbabwe, endowed with world-class tourism assets from the majestic Victoria Falls and the ancient Great Zimbabwe Ruins to Matopos Hills, Chinhoyi Caves and the evergreen Eastern Highlands can replicate this innovation by embedding those tourism destinations within studios for a one-stop-filming production. Such integrated studios would transform natural heritage sites into handy active filming locations, significantly reducing logistical costs, cutting production time and positioning Zimbabwe as a premier film and content creation destination in Africa.

Equally impressive is NRTV's deployment of a proprietary Chinese AI model, which has revolutionized its newsgathering and dissemination. Powered by AI-assisted editing, automated transcription and intelligent content distribution, the station now publishes over, 600 news stories daily across broadcast and social media platforms, fully aligned with China's modernization drive for efficient, data-driven journalism.

This technological leap offers immense lessons for Zimbabwe. The adoption of advanced Chinese AI solutions can directly empower Zimbabwean Media Houses, University Media Faculties and content creators, while accelerating the broader national vision of Digitalising Zimbabwe. This aligns seamlessly with Zimbabwe's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched by His Excellency President Dr Emmerson Dambudzo Mnangagwa in March this year, as the Strategy provides a comprehensive framework for driving digital transformation, innovation and sustainable growth towards an Upper Middle-Income Economy by 2030 leaving no one and no place behind.

text:
He came from Sri Lanka to defend Ukraine. His final words were: "Jelo, I’m having trouble breathing."

Shehan Ranishka was born in Sri Lanka and had served in its national army.

When Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began, he heard President Zelenskyy’s call to people around the world—and made his decision.

He told his mother that this was unjust, that Putin had no right to act this way, and that he would do everything in his power for the Ukrainian people.

In Ukraine, Shehan—who adopted the call sign "Dentist"—became someone his fellow soldiers called "brother."

He fought on the front lines, held positions, took part in assaults, and sustained wounds—yet every time, he returned to the fight.

He dreamed of bringing Sri Lankan special forces to Ukraine. And he succeeded—though not with everyone.

Then came some news, which he delivered with a wry smile: "I have two pieces of news. The good news is that we’re famous. The bad news is that we’re now wanted men—both in Russia and in Sri Lanka."

He formed his own unit of Sri Lankans—a small army within the larger army, complete with its own uniforms, traditions, and people.

In Ukraine, he found a second family. Alina met him in a hospital while assisting with translation; that professional collaboration gradually evolved into a close friendship. He called her parents "Dad" and "Mom," and called her "Princess" or "Wednesday"—sometimes jokingly referring to her as his sister.

He grew very fond of Kharkiv, especially the Central Park, and dreamed of seeing the city in its peaceful beauty.

He dreamed of obtaining Ukrainian citizenship, working for Ukrainian civil airlines, and buying a home in Kharkiv.

He had even arranged a burial plot for himself—right next to his fallen commander, Taras Buntar.

He requested that, in the event of his death, funds be donated to orphanages for children from Kharkiv and the surrounding region who had lost their parents during the war.

On December 4, 2023, near the village of Andriivka in the Kupiansk sector, he and his fellow soldier, Lahiru, set out to recover the body of a fallen comrade from Sri Lanka.

A heavy mortar barrage began. Shehan was wounded. Lahiru provided first aid, applying a tourniquet.

The last thing Shehan asked for was water. Then he said, "Jelo, I’m finding it very hard to breathe; I’m so cold."

Lahiru urged the medics to speed up the evacuation, but since he did not speak Ukrainian—and the Ukrainian side did not understand English—this became a major difficulty.

Shehan died in his arms.

He was laid to rest in the Rivne region, beside the commander he considered his own—just as he had wished.

His mother, Mrs. Tamara, learned all of this only after her son’s death.

She thanked Lahiru for everything he had done for her son. He expressed gratitude to Lina, a combat medic who was close to him. He also thanked Alina and her parents for becoming a family to him when his own relatives were abroad.

In return, his mother was told something that not every mother gets to hear: "You raised not just a warrior, but, above all, a human being—someone with whom one could share everything, someone who would always offer support and lead the way by his own example."

Shehan went to defend Ukraine, even though it was not his own land. And for it, he gave the most precious thing he had—his life.

His story, his name, and his face will remain in the memories of those who knew him—and in the memory of the country he defended as if it were his own.

Former British soldier Daniel Khalife escaped twice while awaiting trial on charges of espionage in 2023.

Khalife, whose mother is Iranian, joined the British Army in September 2018 and was assigned to the 16th Signal Regiment in Stafford after receiving a security clearance and more than a year of specialized training.

In 2019 Khalife contacted an Iranian man connected to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. Khalife provided at least one classified document which he later claimed was a fake and collected a payment of £1,500 from a dead drop in Mill Hill Park in London. He also collected identifying information on Army personnel from a database to pass to Iran.

However, Khalife then contacted MI6 through their website saying he was in touch with the Iranian government and offered to work as a double agent.

In January 2023, he was confined to his Army barracks while under investigation. He escaped after rigging a fake explosive device in his room, apparently to hamper and delay a response to his disappearance. Khalife was captured in the nearby town of Stone and remanded into police custody.

While being held in HMD Wandsworth prison awaiting trial, he made another daring escape on September 6th, 2023. After being assigned to kitchen duties, he tied himself to the undercarriage of a food delivery truck using bedsheets and successfully passed through the prison gates and out into London before rolling out from underneath the truck at a traffic light and fleeing on foot. Fellow inmate Adeel Khan helped him plan the escape and arranged for him to receive £400 in cash from someone in London.

Khalife remained on the run for three days, buying new clothing and a cell phone with cash, and appeared on CCTV footage at several locations around London. He stayed in touch with Adeel Khan throughout by borrowing the cell phones of bystanders. On September 9th he was captured by a plainclothes Metropolitan Police detective sergeant while riding a bicycle on a footpath in Northolt.

Khalife was found guilty of espionage in November 2024 and later sentenced to more than fourteen years in prison.

A woman was found dead at her marital home in Bihar's Begusarai district after allegedly facing harassment over dowry and pressure to convert to Islam, according to a complaint filed by her mother.

The family has accused her husband, Mohammad Arzoo, of strangling her to death.

Police have registered a case and are investigating the allegations.

The woman, Ankita Kumari, married Arzoo in 2021 after the two eloped. Following their marriage, Ankita's family filed a police complaint against Arzoo. However, as both were adults, a court allowed them to live together. They subsequently began living as husband and wife.

According to Ankita’s mother, Draupadi Devi, tensions between the couple started to surface right after their marriage because of the couple’s different religious backgrounds. The situation, according to her, worsened after Ankita gave birth to a daughter in 2023.

Draupadi alleged that Arzoo and his family began demanding money as dowry and pressuring Ankita to convert to Islam. She claimed her daughter was repeatedly harassed for refusing to change her religion and failing to meet the alleged dowry demands.

As the matter escalated, Ankita’s family intervened and tried to resolve the dispute through discussions. She even came back to her parental home. However, after mediation, Ankita returned to live with her husband.

Her mother further said that the harassment over dowry and religious conversion continued.

On October 19, Ankita asked her husband to take her to a Durga temple in Badi Ballia to offer prayers during Dussehra. According to her mother, Arzoo became angry and assaulted her.

Draupadi said Ankita spoke to her around 11 pm that night and expressed a desire to return to her parental home again. At around 2 am, Arzoo informed the family that Ankita had died by suicide by hanging.

Her family reached the village the following day and lodged a complaint at the local police station on October 20. The complaint named Arju, his brother, the brother's wife, his sister and another person. The family accused them of dowry-related harassment, pressuring Ankita to convert and murdering her.

Police took custody of Ankita's body and sent it for a postmortem examination before handing it over to her family.

Senior cop Nikhil Kumar confirmed that a case had been registered on the complaint filed by Draupadi Devi and an investigation has begun.

text:
@LeTourFemmes #TDFF2027
The Chaîne des Puys is a north-south chain of roughly 80 monogenetic volcanoes (cinder cones, lava domes, and maars) that erupted between about 95,000 and 8,600 years ago.

There were phases of block-and-ash flows, phreatomagmatic activity, and a final summit eruption around 10,700 years ago after a short pause that allowed some vegetation to recolonize. Growth likely occurred over decades, comparable to modern examples such as Mount St. Helens. It is a classic Peléan-type lava dome and was later tilted slightly by further intrusion.

The volcanic nature of the Puys was first clearly recognized in 1751 by Jean-Étienne Guettard. The site remains slowly evolving under erosion, occasional rockfalls, and lahars, but is dormant. 

In pre-Christian times the summit served as a place for spiritual ceremonies and assemblies. A Gallo-Roman Temple of Mercury (Mercurius Dumias / Mercury of the Dôme) occupied the site.

A first temple was built around 50 CE (arkose construction); it was replaced around 140–150 CE by a larger trachyte temple lower on the slope. This was one of the largest mountain temples in Roman Gaul (covering about 3,600 m² on terraced platforms totaling roughly 60 m × 60 m), combining Celtic and classical features (square cella with gallery and pronaos).

It was a major pilgrimage center overlooking Augustonemetum (Clermont-Ferrand), accessible via a Roman road (the later mule-drivers’ path). Coins and finds indicate use into the 4th–5th centuries before abandonment and ruin.

The ruins were rediscovered in 1872 during meteorological observatory construction. Excavations followed (notably 1873–1878, 1901–1906, and 2000–2004), revealing a bronze dedication tablet and a Mercury statuette. It was classified a Monument Historique in 1889.
A major TDF television/radio antenna has stood on the summit since 1956.

A steam railway using the Hanscotte central-rail system ran from Place Lamartine in Clermont-Ferrand to near the summit (1907–1926). It was replaced by a toll road (opened 1926), which carried heavy car traffic until restricted.

In 2012 the electric rack railway Panoramique des Dômes (about 5 km) opened, closing the road to general vehicles to protect the fragile summit environment while allowing high visitor numbers.

 Hiking paths remain, including the historic mule-drivers’ trail. In 1908 the Michelin brothers offered a large prize (100,000 francs) for the first powered flight from the Paris region to the summit with a passenger, after circling Clermont’s cathedral, in under six hours. Eugène Renaux and passenger Albert Senouque achieved it on 7 March 1911 in a Farman biplane (roughly 5 hours 10 minutes), landing on the rocky summit.

Today the summit draws roughly 400,000–500,000 visitors annually, offering panoramic views of the Chaîne des Puys and Clermont-Ferrand. It is popular for paragliding, cycling (frequent Tour de France stage), and scientific tourism.

The area is managed for sustainable access under Grand Site de France principles. The department’s volcanic identity, scientific legacy, and Roman heritage make the Puy de Dôme one of France’s most iconic natural and cultural landmarks.
