text:
SCP-103: Rhys' Head/Mara's Heart

SCP-103 starts with a man being kept alive and a colleague who cannot accept that saving him may already be impossible. Dr. Ewan Mara has stomach cancer. During an aggressive experimental treatment, his stomach is replaced by an extradimensional rift, and his research partner, Dr. Jacob Rhys, takes charge of studying what has happened.

The situation is horrific before anyone starts testing it. Mara is unconscious, parts of his body are disappearing, and the space where his stomach should be absorbs whatever enters it. Rhys keeps approaching the problem as something he can fix if he finds the right experiment. Every setback becomes another reason to keep going.

There are signs early on that he should not be running this project. A member of the medical staff offers grief counseling. Concerns reach the Ethics Committee. Rhys insists his involvement is professional, but the way he speaks to Mara when other people leave tells a different story. He keeps promising that he can bring him back.

One attempt binds the rift to Mara's body, preventing it from spreading beyond him. That succeeds as containment. It does not restore the organs already consumed or stop the rift from consuming more of him. The distinction is unbearable for Rhys, who wanted a treatment and instead gets a way to keep the disaster confined to his friend.

Then the Foundation starts disposing of nuclear waste through the opening. That's an ugly turn. A living person's condition becomes useful to the institution, while the researcher responsible for him keeps searching for reasons to call the next experiment a possible cure. The paperwork can label an outcome successful even as Mara's body continues disappearing.

The personal details make this much harder to shrug off. Mara has a wife who still writes and a young son imagining a quest for a potion that will wake his father. Rhys talks about them beside the bed. Those little pieces of an ordinary life keep cutting through the clinical language of the file.

His final major attempt uses Mara's own research. It fails too. Afterward, Rhys finally talks openly about his fear of being powerless around illness and admits that he made a terrible decision because he wasn't ready to say goodbye. The story lets that explanation be understandable without making everything he did acceptable.

By the end, Mara is dead, the anomaly is neutralized, and Rhys is missing. The file gives us evidence of what was left behind, but no confirmed account of where Rhys went. That uncertainty matters. What the entry does show clearly is someone losing the ability to separate helping another person from needing his own efforts to succeed. Every additional chance he insists on giving Mara costs Mara more.

Pixel Matrix Faceplate: Software V1.2, 24-Month Warranty, and Free Replacement

Hi everyone,

Recently, many of you raised concerns about how the Pixel Matrix Faceplate writes to its internal storage, and some of you investigated it in detail. You were right to raise it, and thank you for the work you put in. We’re sorry for the trouble along the way.

What’s going on
In the original software, the Clock and Performance screens redrew the display every second, and every redraw was saved to the faceplate’s storage. Over long periods of use, that wears the storage faster than it should.

Uploading an image, static or animated, writes it to storage once. Displaying it afterwards doesn’t wear the storage, so occasional uploads are fine. The problem was screens that redraw every second.

What we’re doing
1. Software V1.2, available now
Please start by installing V1.2. It cuts unnecessary redraws and fixes several issues you reported:

● Clock no longer redraws every second: the colon stays on, and the progress bar adds one dot per minute.
● Do Not Disturb (off by default): CPU, GPU and RAM readouts hold steady unless they change by more than 6 percentage points. FPS keeps updating.
● Real in-game FPS in the Composite and Performance layouts, verified on SteamOS 3.9.4.
● Brightness is capped and bright animations run at a lower frame rate, to stay within what the USB port can supply. This stops the brightness swings during gaming and reduces flicker.
● The display turns off before your Steam Machine sleeps and comes back on wake.
● New settings for time zone, 12/24-hour clock, temperature unit, and weather location.

Download V1.2 and full release notes: https://t.co/sGOUW9zdJj

2. Warranty extended from 18 to 24 months
Your Pixel Matrix Faceplate is now covered for 24 months. If a display issue shows up during that time, email support@jsaux.com and we’ll replace it free.

3. Free replacement if you’re still concerned
If you still have concerns after updating, we’ll send you a new faceplate from our latest hardware revision, free of charge. The new faceplate stores the clock and performance layouts on board and only receives the numbers from your Steam Machine, so updating them doesn’t write to storage. The new faceplate's firmware can also be updated over USB-C.

Email support@jsaux.com with the subject “Pixel Matrix Replacement”, your order number, and your shipping address. We’ll reply to confirm your details. Replacements start shipping in early November, in the order requests come in. You don’t need to send your current faceplate back.

Some of you heard from our support team that we’d mail you a programming tool to update the firmware yourself. Because that would mean opening the faceplate and connecting the tool to the internal board, the process is fairly involved. To save you the trouble, we’ve decided to offer a free replacement instead.

4. Hardware improvements for new units
Every faceplate shipping from November onward uses the new hardware: clock and performance updates don’t write to storage, firmware can be updated over USB-C, and the USB-C port has current limiting. New units need no action. If your order hasn’t shipped yet, it will ship with the new hardware.

Thanks for choosing us. Questions? Reply here or email support@jsaux.com. We read every message.

The JSAUX Team

text:
Hermes yesterday: three features moved out of core into plugins, and the move already shipped in v0.22.5, out overnight. If Claude Desktop, Cursor or Claude Code launch hermes mcp serve, that command now exits with a pointer: install the mcp-serve plugin and change the args to mcp-serve; hermes import-agent and hermes claw need agent-importers; Singularity users get their plugin installed for them. Also: subagents can now be routed per task to a named model or a Hermes profile. 190 commits landed on main; here are the 10 that matter.

1️⃣ Three features leave core: mcp serve, import-agent and Singularity

Before: Hermes as an MCP server (hermes mcp serve), hermes import-agent, the OpenClaw migration (hermes claw and the openclaw-migration skill) and the Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend were built into core. After: each lives in an official catalog plugin, and the old commands print where they went. hermes mcp serve exits with the new spelling and the install line on stderr, never on the MCP wire; nothing installs mcp-serve for you, because no Hermes config records which MCP clients launch it, so install it with hermes plugins install mcp-serve and change the client's args to mcp-serve; the ten tool names stay the same. hermes import-agent and hermes claw point to the agent-importers plugin; it installs itself only on homes with a registered import sync source, and a first-time hermes setup now offers to import from OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex CLI or Cursor when it finds one, installing the plugin only after a yes. Singularity keeps its backend name and config keys: hermes update installs the plugin once for every profile that uses it, the next agent or gateway start does it for the active profile (security.allow_lazy_installs still applies), and under plugins.isolation: host it refuses and names the setting to change.

2️⃣ Subagents can be routed per task to a model or a profile

Before: every subagent followed the one delegation section in config.yaml or inherited the parent's model. After: delegation.backend picks a delegation backend, and the default changes nothing (the delegate_task tool definition is byte-identical). With the new advanced-delegation plugin (item 10), Model routes gives the agent named options, each with its own provider, model, reasoning effort and speed tier, to pick per task, and Profile routes runs a task as another Hermes profile, with that profile's model, credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy. /delegation switches the mode for one session or with --global, and Desktop Settings > Model > Subagents gets a Routing section with a mode picker, a route editor and Install or Turn on buttons. It fails closed: when the saved mode's plugin is missing or off, subagents are refused with the fix named, never quietly run on Default, and a task its route cannot serve is refused alone while its siblings run. Limits: profile routes are refused inside managed workers such as Kanban, the Desktop page does not show a session's /delegation override, and a package-managed install refuses the writes. Plugin slash commands can now also ask you to pick an option: buttons on Telegram, Discord and Slack, a numbered list on other messaging platforms, a picker in the CLI, TUI and Desktop.

3️⃣ Edge TTS speaks again

Before: since about October 13, Microsoft's speech endpoint rejected the token that the pinned edge-tts 7.2.7 sends, so every Edge synthesis failed with a 403. Edge is Hermes's default free voice (tts.provider: edge), so voice replies broke for anyone on the default. After: Hermes pins edge-tts 7.3.1, which sends the new token, and a live synthesis produced audio with no 403.

4️⃣ Pillow 13 closes three critical image-decoder holes

Before: Hermes shipped Pillow 12.3.0, a core dependency that resizes images for the vision tools, with 28 open advisories and no 12.x backport. Three are critical: a heap overflow decoding JPEG, a heap overflow saving TIFF to a buffer and a Ghostscript argument injection; 16 more are high. After: Pillow 13.0.0. browser-harness still pins 12.3.0, so Hermes overrides it; its contact sheets, thumbnails and click overlays came out pixel-identical. A plugin that asks for Pillow below 13 also gets 13.0.0.

5️⃣ Desktop moves to Electron 44, and leaves macOS 11, macOS 12 and 32-bit Windows

Before: the desktop app ran Electron 40.10.2, which sits inside two GitHub security advisories (the high one has no fixed 40.x release) and still trusts the eMudhra root behind eight compromised intermediate certificates disclosed on October 20. It stayed there because newer Electron broke the installer's desktop build on Windows machines without the VC++ runtime. After: Electron 44.9.3, outside both advisories and no longer trusting that root; on Windows the build copies the runtime DLL that ships with Hermes's own Python, with nothing installed system-wide. Heads-up: Electron 44 does not run on macOS 11, macOS 12 or 32-bit Windows, so the desktop app ends support there. Not tested yet: anything on macOS (notifications included), the PDF preview and a full installer run on a fresh Windows machine. Microsoft Store app with v0.22.5, the .exe and .dmg app with its next bundled release.

6️⃣ Fresh Desktop installs get onboarding and the free trial back

Before: since the unified gateway in v0.22.1, the gateway decided whether it was serving the Desktop on this machine from settings only a Desktop-launched backend had, so a new user landed on the provider picker with no free account and onboarding never started; Settings > Advanced > Run onboarding again opened nothing, and quitting before onboarding lost the trial. After: the Desktop declares itself on each connection, accepted only with a native control ticket so a remote or tunnelled client never gets the trial; a fresh install gets its free account and onboarding again. Once claimed, the trial model also runs cron jobs, Kanban workers, side agents and the CLI when no model is set, and a chat started on the trial moves to the provider you connect later. The provider picker no longer shows a grey box of CLI commands to someone who has not set up a provider.

7️⃣ A chat whose folder is gone says so

Before: when a chat's working folder was deleted, every message came back as The model request failed, Something went wrong. On the classic CLI, /goal burned its 20-turn budget in about 40 seconds judging those refusals, and safe-mode or config-only chats parked every later message behind a lost run, even after the folder came back. After: the turn is refused before it runs, and the reply names the folder and the way out: recreate it, /worktree new in the CLI or Move to project in Desktop. A refused turn never drives /goal or a /loop --until judge, and nothing is saved for a turn that never ran.

8️⃣ Usage-window plans: one bar per allowance

New for Nous subscriptions whose included usage is tracked as allowances (today, this week, this month, a separate one for large models) instead of a credit balance. /usage shows one bar per allowance with percent used and time to reset, and Desktop Billing adds gauges and a Keep going on credits setting. Model pickers list the plan's recommended models first and tag them Large or Free. At a limit, the message names the allowance, when it resets and what still works; Hermes never switches models on its own and skips the fallback chain, and with a credential pool only the refused model is benched. Hermes only shows what the server sends, and only on Nous routes: other plans and providers see no change.

9️⃣ Desktop: mute the chimes, drag to pin, install with +

Settings > Notifications > Sounds gains Mute interface sounds, which silences the completion, wake and thinking sounds, haptics and the sound of OS notifications (the banners still show), plus None in the completion-sound picker. Drag a session onto Pinned to pin it and back out to unpin. In the Capabilities catalog, install is a one-way + button, an installed entry gets its on/off switch and Uninstall sits in its detail; the install dialog now shows the real tier (Official, Verified or Community) instead of calling every pick Verified, and the switch and + on compact cards act instead of opening the details. Gateway group chats show which bot is working again.

🔟 1 new plugin in the catalog: the delegation routes

One new entry, and it is official: advanced-delegation, the plugin behind item 2's Model routes and Profile routes, plus hermes delegation config and /delegation. It has no Python dependencies and makes no network or model calls of its own, and it writes only delegation.backend and delegation.backends in the active profile's config.yaml. Heads-up: a model route's optional api_key is stored in config.yaml in plain text, and listing a profile under profile routes lets this profile's subagents use that profile's credentials, SOUL.md and terminal policy. It needs v0.22.5; on an older core it loads, logs a warning and registers nothing. Catalog entries do not wait for a release: they go live once the published catalog refreshes.

• Delegation: advanced-delegation

━━━━━━━━━━

⚙️ Meanwhile, in the engine room

Dozens of fixes landed yesterday that most users never see, and most of them polished the new delegation routing and usage-window plans before they merged.

• Windows updates from v0.22.4 get the new launcher and an install stamp at the new commit, instead of keeping the old hermes.exe on Python 3.14.7 after the same day's Python repin: Windows will not delete the launcher that is running the update, so it is now renamed aside and collected later. The v0.22.5 release-candidate tests caught it before the release
• Stable-channel installs whose sessions already use the gateway runtime are held at their build instead of being offered v0.22.2 and then refused as a downgrade on every hermes update; Desktop, the dashboard and hermes update --check now say held
• The API server's /v1/chat/completions reports finish_reason length for a turn that hit agent.max_turns instead of cancelled, which brokers read as an abort and threw away a usable answer; retrying a rate-limited call no longer draws a this looks like a loop warning
• terminal with background=true on Docker, SSH, Modal and other non-local backends said Background process started even when the launch failed (no bash in the image, sandbox gone); it now returns the real error, and background launches honour workdir

If you noticed none of this, it worked.

Everything above already shipped in v0.22.5, out overnight (Desktop app changes reach the Microsoft Store app now and the .exe and .dmg app with its next bundled release). Latest stable: v0.22.5.

Which one hits you most? 👇

text:
Scientists May Have Found a Way to Wake Up Sleeping Hair Follicles — And Regrow Lost Hair!

Scientists are testing an experimental treatment called PP405 that could offer a new approach to hair loss. Unlike traditional treatments that mainly focus on slowing hair loss or supporting existing hair growth, PP405 targets the energy-producing processes inside dormant hair follicle stem cells, aiming to switch them back into an active growth state.

In a Phase 2a clinical trial involving 78 men and women with pattern hair loss, participants applied PP405 or a placebo to their scalps daily for four weeks. The results offered an encouraging sign: among men with more advanced hair loss, 31% of those who received PP405 experienced an increase in hair density of more than 20% by week eight. That was four weeks after they had stopped using the treatment. No participants in the placebo group achieved the same level of improvement.

But there’s another reason researchers are interested in this treatment. The findings suggest that hair growth may be possible in areas where hair was no longer visibly present. This raises an exciting possibility: some areas of a thinning scalp may still contain hair follicles with the potential to become active again.

The early safety results were also encouraging. PP405 was well tolerated during the study, and researchers detected no measurable amount of the drug entering participants’ bloodstreams. However, the trial was small, and the results do not yet prove that the treatment will work for everyone or produce lasting results.

Developed by Pelage Pharmaceuticals, PP405 is still experimental. Larger clinical trials are needed to establish how effective it is, how long the results last, and which people are most likely to benefit.

Could waking up dormant hair follicles become the next major breakthrough in treating baldness? Researchers are now working to find out.

Source: Pelage Pharmaceuticals, Positive Phase 2a Clinical Trial Results for PP405 in Regenerative Hair Loss Therapy (2025).

text:
🔴WAR ON TERRORISM: IRAN 🇮🇷🔴/Times of Israel/

Report: IDF chief says no operational need for strike on Iran before Israeli election

According to Channel 13, Zamir says ‘no indications’ of need for military action, but army would act if necessary; tensions rise as Tehran reports fresh tanker attacks in Hormuz

Hamas-led onslaught, at Zikim Base in southern Israel on October 5, 2026. (Israel Defense Forces)

IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir said during a recent private meeting that he does not currently see an operational need to strike Iran before next week’s Knesset election, Channel 13 reported on Thursday.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been accused by critics of pushing for a renewal of the war against Iran to influence or delay the October 27 vote — a charge he has denied.

“We do not see any indications of a need to strike Iran before the election. If we determine that a strike on Iran is necessary, we will carry it out,” Zamir was quoted as saying.

Netanyahu’s main rival, Yashar chief Gadi Eisenkot, offered a similar message publicly earlier Thursday, telling Channel 13: “There is no direct, immediate threat from Iran that necessitates a war prior to the election.”
Shipping attacks add to tensions

The comments came as tensions continued to build in the region.

Seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz overnight after being hit by Iran or striking naval mines, Tehran said Thursday, a markedly high number as tensions rise over concerns about a return to all-out war.

Iranian state television reported the claims about the latest attacks on ships, which the Associated Press said it couldn’t independently confirm.

The report cited the Revolutionary Guard Corps navy, which again threatened to strike US military bases in the region if the US keeps helping guide commercial ships through the strait.

The report didn’t mention casualties. Iran still asserts control over the waterway, a central point of leverage in any talks with the US over the war.

October has had the most reported attacks on commercial shipping since March, during the war’s opening weeks, according to a British military monitor, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations.

UKMTO didn’t report the latest attacks, but it has noted new reluctance by some shippers to report incidents.

Oil producers have found ways to keep crude flowing, experts say, but at a mounting cost.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday said that a wary Tehran remains open to diplomacy, but is ready to defend itself.

Iran has warned that it has learned important military lessons from the war that began with US and Israeli attacks on February 28.

In recent days, Tehran has indicated that it could expand targets to include infrastructure such as undersea cables and data centers.

The United States, for its part, is sending more military assets to the region, including a third aircraft carrier and thousands of troops, to join the largest force of American warships and aircraft in the Middle East in decades.

Mediators have continued trying to bring Washington and Tehran back to formal negotiations.

Iran has promoted a proposal that would end the war and fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if the United States accepts several conditions, including ending its blockade of Iranian ports, easing restrictions on Iranian oil exports, releasing frozen assets and ending hostilities on all fronts.

A similar agreement signed in June collapsed within days. Trump rejected Tehran’s latest seven-day proposal in late September, though both sides have acknowledged that indirect discussions have continued.

Reports of plans for strikes after midterms

The United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed military strikes on Iran following the November 3 US midterm elections, The New York Times reported Wednesday, citing US officials and others briefed on the matter.

The report said the two countries had stepped up military exercises ahead of a possible “short but intensive operation,” including Israeli flyovers near Iran intended to simulate strike maneuvers.

Potential targets were said to include Iranian nuclear facilities, energy infrastructure and missile and drone arsenals.

Recent reports have said Netanyahu is eager to renew strikes on Iran but has been restrained by Trump, who has signaled that he prefers to wait until after the midterms.

Netanyahu on Thursday denied reports about such discussions as “incorrect” and declined to detail his conversations with Trump.

On October 9, Trump said Washington would not strike Iran before the US vote, while a separate report said Zamir had warned American generals that an attack in the coming weeks could force Israel’s October 27 election to be postponed because Iran would likely respond with massive missile fire at Israel.

text:
You do have to separate two groups of reservists here. 

Being a reservist doing your training days, year after year and be battle ready just in case…..or those who are reservists that do the same as the first group but actually deploy to operations. 

The first group don’t need any of the above needs met you mentioned, except for military medical. The deployed reservist do get compensated within their pay package to reflect their disadvantage of being reservists. 

Having said all that, being a reservist or regular has one main feature difference. Reservist offer their service and be called in to do a job if needed, hence the word reservist. Regulars don’t, you do the job you get trained and paid for and if you don’t like it, leave the military.

And let us not get into the weeds about the different services. The three branches/services have perks (or not, depends how you view them) the others do not. Royal Navy, Army and the RAF are differently structured in setup as well as in management of them so to speak. All three will never be comparable to each other.

One example I can speak of, as it is widely known are RAF armourers. When government decided to make them equal in pay in all three services, the upheaval was enormous. They were paid so much more (including in their bands) than the army or navy, many of them decided to leave the RAF. Literally. I worked with some of the guys in civvie  street hence I know.

I have to be very careful how I word things in public. My language is simple and non military, plus my experience as an army wife, a so called dependant, I will not talk shop on a public platform about the many things I know or came across.

INDIAN NAVY TO HOST INDO-PACIFIC REGIONAL DIALOGUE 2026 TO EXPLORE SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND ACADEMIC COOPERATION @indiannavy @SpokespersonMoD
@rajnathsingh @DefenceMinIndia
Three-day conference in New Delhi from 03 to 05 Nov 2026 to bring together experts from 18 countries; deliberations to focus on academic networks, maritime science, ocean governance, climate resilience, and emerging technologie

Hon’ble Raksha Mantri, Shri Rajnath Singh, will deliver the Commemorative Address 

on Day 2 Special address by Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon’ble Minister of State (with independent charge) Science and Technology
Over a three-day period spanning 03, 04 and 05 Nov 2026, the Indian Navy will conduct the 2026 edition of the ‘Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue’ (IPRD-2026), which is its annual apex-level international outreach conference pitched at the strategic level, at the Manekshaw Centre, New Delhi.  Organised in close association with the *National Maritime Foundation (NMF), which is the Navy’s knowledge partner and principal organiser of the event, this year’s conference will be centred upon the theme Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific

Successive editions of this annual dialogue have examined a variety of dimensions of the seven deeply-interconnected maritime lines-of-thrust of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI), which had been promulgated by India’s Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi at the 14th East Asia Summit (EAS) in Bangkok in Nov of 2019.  Importantly, the IPOI provides first-order specificity to India’s maritime vision of MAHASAGAR Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. Each edition of the IPRD seeks to provide second- and third-order specificity to the country’s maritime policy by translating the IPOI’s broad framework for cooperation into specific, actionable proposals.

The choice of this year’s theme reflects a fundamental feature of the contemporary maritime domain: the oceans are interconnected, but the scientific knowledge, technological capabilities and institutions required to understand and manage them remain unevenly distributed.  Care is being taken to ensure that the word ‘science’ is not allowed to be restricted to the ‘physical’ sciences alone, (which have traditionally encompassed ‘engineering’ and ‘technology’ the latter being ‘applied engineering’) but also incorporate the ‘life sciences, as also the ‘social sciences’.  Thus, the multifarious facets of climate change, maritime trade, the maritime ramifications of supply- and value-chains and their vulnerabilities, the ever-increasing pressure upon marine resources, and the growing threats to critical maritime infrastructure, will all form important elements of the conference.  Given that all these elements transcend national boundaries, effective responses require not merely more sophisticated technologies but stronger arrangements for cooperation, information-sharing, and the development of human capital.   

The three days of this year’s conference will incorporate five professional thematic sessions.  These professional sessions will address ‘Academic Networks, Research, and Human Capital Development’; ‘Maritime Situational Awareness and Protection of Critical Maritime Infrastructure’; ‘Oceanographic Science and Climate Resilience’; ‘Collaborative Approaches to Ocean Governance and Maritime Resilience’; and ‘Transformative Maritime Technologies and Dual-Use Implications’.  The deliberations will consider practical pathways for joint research, collaborative technology development, responsible governance, appropriate access to scientific data, and stronger institutional partnerships.

#IPRD2026 will also feature two ‘special’ sessions.  The first of these, entitled, ‘Perspectives from the Flag Bridge’, will bring together former naval chiefs from India and Sri Lanka, to offer 1/2

text:
HOAC Foods India: From a regional staples business to an organised, omnichannel FMCG platform. 🌾

HOAC Foods India Limited, operating under the HOAC and Hari Om brands, is building a business around everyday food consumption - fresh flour, spices, edible oils, pulses and other household staples. What makes the story interesting is the combination of product expansion, distribution reach and improving financial performance. 

The company increased its portfolio from 150 SKUs in FY22–23 to 235 SKUs in FY25–26, a 56.7% expansion. 

Fresh flour remains its core business, while healthy flour contributed 49% of revenue, spices and rice accounted for 35%, edible oils and pulses contributed 14%, and the newer ready-to-eat category made up the remaining 2%.

The financial performance has been strong. Revenue increased from ₹26.48 crore in FY24–25 to ₹50.11 crore in FY25–26, representing 89.26% growth. EBITDA rose 71.91% to ₹7.31 crore, while profit after tax increased 77.45% to ₹4.41 crore. EPS improved from ₹6.79 to ₹10.44, and net worth grew 120.62% to ₹25.12 crore. The EBITDA margin, however, moderated from approximately 16.6% to 14.6%, which is worth monitoring as the business scales. Growth is impressive, but sustaining margins while expanding distribution and product categories will be equally important.

Distribution is central to the company's strategy. HOAC operates through company-owned stores, franchise outlets, B2B retail, digital ordering and exports. Its physical network includes 23 outlets, while B2B distribution reaches more than 4,000 kirana stores. B2B retail contributed 52.34% of the business mix, followed by company outlets at 21.83%, franchise outlets at 18.65% and exports at 7.18%. The company also reported more than 10,200 mobile-application downloads. Its wider portfolio has encouraged cross-category purchases, with average cart value rising from ₹520 in FY22–23 to ₹730 in FY25–26. The opportunity is to use this distribution network to increase repeat purchases and improve the economics of serving each customer.

The next phase is about manufacturing capacity and geographic expansion. HOAC acquired approximately 55,000 square feet of land for development of a larger manufacturing facility. Located in Madhya Pradesh, the proposed facility is intended to strengthen production, streamline supply-chain operations and support faster, more efficient deliveries. The company is also investing in automation, packaging technology, process optimisation and retail expansion. International markets offer another avenue for growth: exports have expanded into Australia, the United States, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong, with plans to explore additional markets. Its own-brand products, alongside white-labelled products, provide two routes to participate in this opportunity.

The key question is whether HOAC can convert this growth into a durable competitive advantage. The Indian staples market is fragmented and competitive, with established FMCG brands, regional players and local suppliers fighting for shelf space and customer loyalty. 

HOAC's potential strengths lie in its local sourcing, processing capabilities, product breadth, distribution relationships and ability to serve both retail and institutional customers. But a wider SKU portfolio and a larger network also bring inventory complexity, working-capital requirements and execution risks. 

Investors should watch cash-flow generation, receivable days, inventory turnover, margin sustainability, capacity utilisation and returns on expansion capital.

HOAC's story is no longer just about selling flour and spices. It is about building a branded, multi-category food business with an expanding distribution and manufacturing backbone.

text:
On this day, Thursday, October 23, 1913, 113 years ago, The Atlanta Constitution reported on its front page (Page 1, Column 2, continued on Page 2, Column 4): "Crowd Conducted Frank Trial, Says Prisoner's Lawyer." Page 7, Column 2 added "Curious Citizens Barred From the Frank Hearing; Many Go to Wrong Place."

Context: Leo M. Frank had been convicted in August 1913 of murdering 13 year old Mary Phagan at the National Pencil Company. On Wednesday, October 22, his lawyers opened their 115 ground motion for a new trial before Judge Leonard S. Roan, in a small anteroom of the state library at the capitol, behind closed doors, with fewer than a dozen people admitted, reporters included.

What the Constitution reported:

Luther Z. Rosser, senior counsel for Frank, declared that the crowd, and not the judge and jury, tried and convicted Frank, and pressed the demonstrations for the solicitor general as reason for a new trial. Forty grounds were argued Wednesday. The session ended at 6 o'clock only because the library closed.

Rosser accused Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey of trying to hang Frank on the smallest pretext: "You would kill him on the dotting of a T or the crossing of a t." Dorsey answered that the defense was "trying to make a mountain of a mole hill." Dorsey was assisted by E. A. Stephens; Rosser and Reuben R. Arnold by Stiles Hopkins and others.

Rosser and Arnold first objected to using the court records at all, saying the stenographers had recorded the arguments inadequately and that only memory would do. It was agreed to use the records. Dorsey said it was "exceedingly strange" that the stenographers had failed to record accurately only the arguments contained in the defense's motion.

On the defense attack on Jim Conley's testimony, Dorsey answered that the objection was not made until twenty-four hours after the testimony was given, and only after the defense had cross-examined Conley. Rosser said: "If this testimony of Conley's is admissible, why, we'll take our medicine."

Dorsey defended the testimony of Mrs. Mattie White, saying her failure to report at once what she had seen at the factory tended to show an effort toward concealment.

When Arnold asked Judge Roan to certify that the jury was near enough to hear courtroom applause, Dorsey said that was a matter for the jurors, not the judge: "We have affidavits from most of them saying they never heard the outbreaks." Rosser broke in: "But the juror won't admit it." Judge Roan recorded his opinion that the jury was within hearing distance. When Rosser declared the crowd had conducted the trial, the solicitor laughed at it.

On Page 7, the paper reported that from 8 o'clock Wednesday morning crowds gathered at the old city hall on Pryor street, expecting to get into the hearing, and were turned away. Deputy Sheriff Plennie Minor guarded the door at the capitol.

The outcome: on October 31, 1913, Judge Roan overruled the motion for a new trial, and the Georgia Supreme Court later affirmed the conviction.

Why this matters:

The defense's claim that a crowd convicted Leo Frank was met by sworn affidavits from the jurors themselves saying they never heard the outbreaks.

Luther Z. Rosser's reply, "But the juror won't admit it," amounted to asking the court to disbelieve the jurors' sworn word.

Frank's lawyers first tried to keep the official record out of the hearing and argue from memory, until it was agreed the records would be used.

Solicitor General Hugh M. Dorsey showed the defense objected to Jim Conley's testimony only twenty-four hours later, after cross-examining him on it.

Dorsey argued Mrs. Mattie White's delay in reporting what she saw at the factory pointed to an effort at concealment.

For all the talk of a mob-run trial, the hearing itself was held behind closed doors, and Judge Roan still denied the motion on October 31, 1913.

Appendix: Full article transcript

Note: Line breaks from the original narrow columns have been joined into paragraphs, and stray quote marks the source uses in place of dashes are shown as commas. A Page 11 professional card that shared the source page is omitted.

The Atlanta Constitution,

Thursday, 23rd October 1913,

PAGE 1, COLUMN 2.

Tried and Convicted by the Courtroom Spectators and Not by the Judge and Jury, Declares Rosser.

TODAY'S HEARING MAY LAST UNTIL MIDNIGHT

Fight Is Bitter Over Conley's Testimony, Defense Declaring That It Should Never Have Been Considered.

Declaring that the crowd and not the judge and jury tried and convicted Leo M. Frank of the murder of Mary Phagan, Luther Rosser, senior counsel for the prisoner, yesterday urged the many demonstrations for the solicitor general as sufficient reason why the convicted superintendent should have another trial.

This was, however, but one of the forty grounds argued Wednesday when the hearing began before Judge Roan in a little anteroom in the state library at the capitol. As 115 objections have been noted to the rulings in the case, it will be several days at least before a decision will be reached.

The proceedings are as tedious as the original trial was dramatic and thrilling. Both the solicitor and counsel for the defense fight bitterly and desperately over every detail.

Wrangling and debate occupied more than two-thirds of the first day's session.

The hearing had hardly begun when Rosser blazed at Solicitor General Dorsey, who prosecuted the prisoner, the charge that he was striving to hang Frank on any pretext, matter not how small: You would kill him on the dotting of a T or the crossing of a t.'

And you, retorted the solicitor, with equally as much display of spirit, are trying to make a mountain of a mole hill.

Forty Clauses Examined.

The entire day was spent in examining forty of the 115 grounds contained in a single volume which the defense offers for a new trial. Neither side seemed to gain much headway. Heated disputes arose over many of the points, and much time was lost in going back over records and history of the case.

The hearing would undoubtedly have run into a night session had it not been for the closing hour at 6 o'clock of the library. Tonight the session will likely be held until midnight or later. It is Judge Roan's expressed wish that the hearing be ended just as early as possible.

A tense battle was staged over the testimony of Jim Conley when the defense presented many parts of his story as grounds for new trial. The fight was entirely as spectacular as the one waged against Conley's story during the trial. The result, however, was the tabling of those particular grounds pertaining to Conley for future examination.

Other grounds that were bones of contention between the prosecution and defense were those that related to testimony at the trial of Frank's immorality. It was while the story told by the Jackson girl of Frank looking into a girl's dressing room while she was disrobing was being discussed that the session came to an end at 6 o'clock.

Hearing Behind Closed Doors.

Solicitor Dorsey was assisted by his assistant, E. A.

Stephens, while Colonel Rosser and Colonel Arnold were aided by Stiles Hopkins and others. The hearing was behind closed doors, less than a dozen persons, including reporters being admitted. It will probably last at least a week, though some say it will come to an end next Saturday.

So far, nothing has been mentioned of the affidavits charging bias against Jurors Johenning and Henslee. No witnesses have been examined. Only forty of the grounds given in the petition for a new trial have been considered.

Each clause is read by the defense. Objection, if there be any, is made by the solicitor. Argument follows. An end of which is the checking of the reason by Judge Roan for future use. It will require probably all of today to finish examining these 115 sections.

An agreement has been made between the two sides to admit any new evidence which might arrive for either defense or prosecution at the time it appears. This was done because both sides expect to obtain new affidavits relative to the jurors. Both Mr. Arnold and Rosser objected vigorously at the opening of the hearing to reference to the records for argument presented by either the defense or solicitor. The stenographers, they declared, had recorded the argument inadequately, and that the only successful manner in which they could go back to argument of any kind during the trial was by memory.

Agree to Use Records.

It was agreed, however, to use the records. This was done after much

Continued on Page Two.

PAGE 2, COLUMN 4

FIGHTS FOR FRANK

Photo by Francis E. Price

HERBERT HAAS. Photographed for Constitution Wednesday while Frank hearing was in progress. He is associated in the case with Arnold and Rosser.

PAGE 2, COLUMN 4

CROWD RAN TRIAL SAY FRANK'S LAWYERS

Continued From Page One.

protest, during which Solicitor Dorsey said: It is a remarkable thing about this business that the court stenographers failed to accurately record any of the important arguments, or, rather, any of those contained in the motion for new trial.

This is the first time I've ever heard of such a thing happening. There isn't a man on earth who could recall those objections and arguments. It is strange, exceedingly strange, if they are not recorded as completely as they should have been. One section objected to the admission as evidence of the talk of Detective Starnes over the telephone with Frank on the morning of the murder's discovery in which Starnes testified at the trial that he was guarded because of importance of the message he was conveying.

Among the other sections considered were the following: The admission of the state's diagram of the pencil factory building to be used as evidence, and which was marked with Greek crosses and dots to outline the state's theory.

The admission of Black's testimony of Frank's conduct on the day of the discovery, which he compared with previous days. The testimony of Black to the effect that counsel had been obtained by the time Frank was first carried to police headquarters.

Argue Over Bloody Shirt.

The failure of the court to admit Newt Lee's admission of owning the bloody shirt as testified to by Witness John Black. The court's failure to exclude a number of questions and answers of Jim Conley's testimony, which, the defense alleged, was highly prejudicial, and which involved transactions far removed from the real issue.

To this particular section, the solicitor answered that objection to Conley's story was not made until twenty-four hours after it was given. Also, that objection was made not until the defense had examined the witness in question.

A long argument lasting hours resulted over this. Colonel Arnold declared that Conley was not cross-examined upon the salacious part of his story, but merely regarding dates and incidents connected with his watching at the first door while Frank was alleged to have entertained girls and women on the office floor.

At the close of the dispute Colonel Rosser said:

If this testimony of Conley's is admissible, why, we'll take our medicine. If not, we have been done a horrible injustice. And we're not going to say we let that particular testimony hang this man. It won't. It can't.

Of the other reasons named in the motion, the first following this dispute to be considered was the section relating to the negro's story. It was an objection to Conley's statement that the had seen Frank in a position with women in which he had never seen any other man with children. Objection was made on the grounds that it was highly prejudicial.

Made Too Late, Says Dorsey.

Dorsey's answer to this was that all objections to Conley were made after the defense had examined him thoroughly.

It was during the presentation of this section that Colonel Arnold accused Dorsey of having been guilty of contempt of court in having violated a rule of Judge Roan's during Conley's examination.

We objected strenuously to any testimony of Frank being in his office with women. We received your ruling, your honor, Dorsey ignored it. It could have been construed that Frank was committing most any crime.

Yes, laughed the judge, maybe such a crime as dancing the tango.

Which would be considerable crime, rejoined the lawyer.

Other reasons were:

Because the court permitted Conley to tell of the trip on which he was taken by the police to interview Frank in the jail, and which he failed to do.

Solicitor Dorsey Objects.

Because Mrs. Mattie White was allowed to take the stand to tell of her conversation with detectives on May 7 when she told of having seen a negro loitering on the first floor of the pencil factory during the afternoon of the murder date.

A strong objection was made to this reason by the solicitor, who said: It was admissible evidence solely because her failure to report it immediately tended to show an effort toward concealment, which undisputedly bore indication of Frank's guilt. Because the court permitted Sheriff Mangum to tell of his conversation with Frank when he strove to obtain the prisoner's permission to talk with Conley in the presence of Chief Beavers and Harry Scott, the Pinkerton man.

Because Dr. Harris was allowed to tell of cabbage tests he had made on other men and to draw his own conclusions before the court of the time Mary Phagan met her death.

Because Jack Dalton was allowed to give testimony of matters and incidents which bore no remote relation to the issue at trial, and the exploitation of which, according to contention, was designed to create prejudice.

A strong plea, in fact, one of the strongest the defense claims in its first volume of grounds, is the record of demonstrations of the crowds during the trial. When these records were offered in the afternoon, Solicitor Dorsey replied: Your honor is thoroughly acquainted with these instances. I have nothing to say of them.

Defense Gains a Point.

After which Mr. Arnold requested Judge Roan to certify that the jury was near enough to hear the applause that rang out at times in the courtroom. Mr. Arnold also suggested a practical demonstration, offering to go to the scene of the trial for such a move.

To this the solicitor answered:

It is a matter of evidence, and should be told by the jurors, not the judge.

Mr. Rosser broke in:

But the juror won't admit it.

We have affidavits from most of them saying they never heard the outbreaks, said Dorsey.

The result was the recording of Judge Roan's opinion that the jury was situated within distance sufficient to hear any of the demonstrations in the courtroom.

The testimony of Herbert Schiff, chief clerk of the pencil factory, was also brought up during the hearing. One of the motion's reasons was based on the colloquies between the solicitor and Schiff, when Dorsey, upon examining the witness from a personal standpoint, announced to the court that he was trying to show the chief clerks feeling in the case.

Tried by Crowd.

It was during the argument over demonstrations in the courtroom that Colonel Rosser declared heatedly that it was his intention to show Judge Roan that it was the crowd and not the judge or jury who conducted the Frank trial and convicted him. This declaration was laughed at by the solicitor.

At the introduction of each section, Judge Roan made particular note of it and also the protest, whenever there was a protest, made by the solicitor. Each of the grounds will be probed before they are taken into consideration. This will take considerable time.

Today's session will begin at 9 o'clock this morning.

PAGE 7, COLUMN 2

Curious Citizens Barred From the Frank Hearing; Many Go to Wrong Place

Surprisingly large numbers of people congregated yesterday in and about the cold city hall on Pryor street, expecting to be admitted to the hearing which they believed to be in progress in the structure on the motion of the attorneys for Leo M. Frank for a new trial.

As early as 8 o'clock Wednesday morning there was a regular stream of men weaving in and out of the old city hall refusing to believe the word of the attendants of the various court rooms that the Frank hearing was not in progress there. The visitors or would-be auditors, continued their vigil during the afternoon hours, but to no avail.

In the crowds which were about the temporary courthouse were seen many of the men who managed to attend the daily sessions of the original Frank trial.

On account of the court being held in the first floor courtroom by Judge Calhoun, the Frank hearing was transferred to the library at the state capitol. The public has been barred from the rooms, only the attorneys on both sides, Judge Roan and the newspaper men engaged in the actual work of following the retrial motions, being admitted. Deputy Sheriff Plennie Minor is on guard at the capitol.

Oil is not merely a commodity in the US-Iran confrontation. It is a strategic instrument of power, and every threat to Gulf energy infrastructure carries costs far beyond the battlefield.

The reported rise in Brent crude to US$116.20 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) to US$102.50 reflects the market's sensitivity to the prospect of expanded US strikes against Iran. The strategic risk extends beyond Iranian production to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf export terminals, refineries and energy infrastructure across the region.

The Strait of Hormuz remains the central vulnerability. Before the conflict, roughly 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products crossed it daily, representing about a quarter of global seaborne oil trade. Alternative pipelines offer only partial relief. Further disruption would raise freight and insurance costs, intensify inflation and expose energy-importing economies, particularly across Asia, to renewed economic pressure.

US President Donald Trump’s threats, Iran’s capacity for asymmetric retaliation, Israeli military planning and attacks by Yemen’s Houthi movement on Saudi targets form a wider escalation risk. Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states face a strategic dilemma: reliance on US security guarantees does not insulate their energy infrastructure from the consequences of US-Iran confrontation.

The costs extend beyond oil producers. Higher energy prices transfer income towards some producers and traders while burdening households, industry and import-dependent economies. Developing countries face particular risks through currency depreciation, higher transport costs and pressure on public finances.

Energy security therefore requires more than military protection of shipping lanes. It demands credible de-escalation, secure maritime access, diversified supply routes and reduced exposure to fossil-fuel price shocks. Without a political settlement, each new threat will sustain a risk premium and make global economic stability hostage to regional escalation.

text:
I asked grok about deployment of the National Guard following federal law over state laws:

It depends on the deployment status (who commands them). The National Guard has a dual state-federal nature.
Three main statuses
•  State Active Duty (SAD): Activated by the governor under state law and state funding. They operate under the governor’s (or state) authority and follow state laws. They can perform law enforcement or support roles if state law allows. The Posse Comitatus Act (which restricts federal military from domestic law enforcement) does not apply.
•  Title 32 status: Hybrid. The governor retains command and control, but the federal government funds the mission (common for training, some domestic support, or federally requested but state-controlled operations). They remain under state authority and generally can assist with law enforcement per state rules. Posse Comitatus usually does not apply because they are not under federal military command.
•  Title 10 (federalized): The president calls them into federal service. Command shifts fully to the federal chain of command (like active-duty forces). They uphold and operate under federal law. They become subject to the Posse Comitatus Act and generally cannot enforce civilian laws domestically unless a specific exception (such as the Insurrection Act) applies.
Key takeaway
•  Under a governor (SAD or Title 32): primarily state authority and state law.
•  Federalized (Title 10): federal authority and federal law.
In the Washington election context from the prior discussion, the offer of unarmed, plainclothes National Guard “Election Neighborhood Watch” observers is under the governor’s state authority (not a federalization), so they would operate under state control and relevant state rules rather than as federal forces.
The exact rules of engagement, powers, and limitations always come from the specific activation orders, applicable state statutes, and federal law for that status.

text:
How many times has WA state govenor offered up National Gaurd to secure ballot boxes and voting locations?

Thought for 15s
Twice: once by Gov. Jay Inslee in 2024 (activation/standby after a ballot-box arson) and once by Gov. Bob Ferguson in October 2026 (an opt-in offer for plainclothes monitoring).⁠Washington Post⁠Komonews

2024 (Gov. Jay Inslee)
Days after an incendiary device damaged or destroyed hundreds of ballots in a Clark County (Vancouver) drop box (linked to a similar incident in Portland, Oregon), Inslee activated Washington National Guard members to standby status for the election week (roughly Nov. 4–7/8). The stated purpose included protecting vital election infrastructure, supporting local law enforcement and the State Patrol, and responding to potential election-related unrest, amid DHS warnings. They were not stationed at drop boxes or voting sites; Washington is all-mail voting, and officials later confirmed the Guard remained on standby and was never deployed to polling locations.⁠ Reuters⁠ Washington Post

2026 (Gov. Bob Ferguson)
Around October 22, 2026, Ferguson sent a letter to county auditors offering to activate unarmed, out-of-uniform National Guard personnel as an “Election Neighborhood Watch.” They would inconspicuously monitor ballot drop boxes or other high-traffic voting areas as “eyes and ears,” coordinate with local authorities if needed, and not interact with voters. Counties could opt in (Thurston County was reported as participating in some coverage). Ferguson cited the 2024 Clark County arson plus recent white-powder letter threats to officials, including the Secretary of State. This expands the Guard’s prior role (cybersecurity support in elections since 2016) to optional physical presence upon county request.⁠Komonews⁠Komonews

No other instances of a Washington governor offering or activating the National Guard specifically to secure ballot boxes or voting locations appear in available reporting. Earlier Guard activations (e.g., 2020 protests, COVID hospital support, Capitol security) were unrelated. The 2026 offer is the first explicit proposal for personnel at drop boxes/voting spots.

text:
TRUMP, PUTIN, AND THE MIDTERMS: PEACE ON SALE BEFORE THE POLLS CLOSE
By @BPartisans 

In Washington, they’re counting votes. In Moscow, they’re counting blows. In Kyiv, they’re counting billions. And in Brussels, those geniuses of subtraction keep writing checks with money they no longer have.

Donald Trump had promised to resolve the Ukrainian conflict with a snap of his fingers. Clearly, the fingers snapped, but the war is still raging. With eleven days to go before the midterms, the U.S. president is discovering an unpleasant truth: Putin isn’t a real estate developer who can be won over with a handshake and a photo in front of a flag.

Trump wants a diplomatic victory to parade as an electoral trophy. Putin wants strategic guarantees. Zelensky wants weapons, billions, and eternal promises. Three men, three agendas, and a war that stubbornly refuses to conform to campaign schedules.

The Kremlin has understood the problem perfectly: Trump is in a hurry. Putin, far less so. Why offer the American billionaire a peace package wrapped in a pretty red ribbon when every additional week potentially increases the pressure on Washington and its European satellites?

In Kyiv, Zelensky is playing his usual tune: more sanctions, more missiles, more money. The Western ATM, however, is starting to display “insufficient funds.” So what! All it takes is a shake-up in Brussels. Over there, leaders have long confused solidarity with automatic debit.

The European Union, that geopolitical retirement home run by teenagers on ideological amphetamines, is already figuring out how to finance the additional 70 billion demanded for 2027. No one seems in a hurry to ask what a political resolution to the conflict might look like. First we borrow; we’ll think about it later. If at all.

Meanwhile, American voters might remind Trump that “America First” didn’t mean “Ukraine Forever.” And if the polls deal him a blow, his grand act as a negotiator could quickly turn into a diplomatic debacle.

The most grotesque aspect remains the West’s obsession with a miracle ceasefire. A pause in the fighting sold as a historic peace, a few handshakes, three triumphant press releases, and everyone goes back to preparing for the next confrontation. Magnificent! We’re repainting the Titanic while it’s sinking.

Because Moscow will not negotiate away its strategic interests to save a majority in Congress. And Trump might discover that the balance of power cannot be shifted by tweets, ultimatums, or favorable polls.

Ultimately, this farce perfectly sums up the contemporary West: Washington wants a victory before the elections, Kyiv wants billions afterward, Brussels wants to pay without understanding, and Moscow is waiting for this whole little world to get over its nervous breakdown.

On November 3, Americans will choose their representatives. Putin will keep his watch. Zelensky will present his bill. And the Europeans, true to their historic role as geopolitical suckers, will discover that they’ve once again earned the right to foot the bill.

text:
In 1946, President Harry Truman's administration unilaterally imposed an arms embargo on Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist (KMT) forces in China, hoping to pressure them into accepting a political compromise with their communist foes.

Chiang had been an important ally during the Second World War and was a friend of the West. But American critics derisively referred to him as “General Cash-My-Check” and argued that supporting the KMT cause was a waste of money.

Whatever his logic, Truman's play for “peace” didn't work. The embargo starved the KMT front lines of supplies, crushed the morale of troops, and paved the way for Mao Zedong's communist takeover of China.

Within a few years, Truman was rushing the Seventh Fleet into the Taiwan Strait to prevent another communist victory against the cornered KMT remnants. Before 1950 was over, American troops were fighting Chinese communist forces in Korea. 36,574 American troops died during this conflict, mostly from fighting the 3 million deployed Chinese troops.

Truman's gambit in the Chinese Civil War had transformed the strategic landscape of Asia in ways he certainly hadn't intended.

Fast-forward to 2026.

President Trump is now aggressively pressuring Ukraine to accept an unfavorable settlement with Russia while holding up critical defensive weapons. Just as Chiang was once mocked as “General Cash-My-Check,” Volodymyr Zelenskyy has been derided by Trump as “P.T. Barnum”.

The isolationist temptation in Washington echoes the failed China policy of the late 1940s: try to strongarm an embattled ally toward compromise with an uncompromising enemy, reduce America's immediate commitments, and hope the geopolitical problem goes away.

But Truman's experience offers a warning. Sometimes the price of standing by a partner looks expensive only because nobody has calculated the cost of abandoning one.

America learned that lesson the hard way in Asia. It shouldn't need to learn it again in Ukraine.

text:
Shapiro’s Russia argument changes how the refinery dispute should be read.

Ben Shapiro says Russia is a geopolitical enemy of the United States and rejects neutrality between Moscow and Kyiv. That position gives his criticism of US pressure a strategic foundation. He is not simply arguing that Ukraine should be free to strike any target; he is questioning why Washington would constrain a partner fighting an adversary it has identified as hostile.

Under Shapiro’s framework, the refinery dispute cannot be reduced to fuel prices. Russian oil infrastructure may have economic significance, but it also belongs to the broader contest between Russia and Ukraine. Limiting Ukraine’s attacks can therefore affect the balance of pressure in the conflict. The key issue becomes whether the restrictions serve a larger American strategy or merely respond to short-term domestic concerns.

Shapiro sees a contradiction in treating Russia as an enemy while pressuring Ukraine to avoid actions that impose costs on Russia. A restriction could still be warranted if it prevented a greater danger, but his account says the cited price rationale is unlikely to succeed. Without a convincing strategic or economic payoff, neutrality risks becoming the default even though the United States is not neutral about the underlying conflict.

The implication is that foreign policy requires consistency between labels and actions. If Russia is an adversary, policy should explain why helping it preserve vulnerable infrastructure advances US interests. If Washington wants restraint from Ukraine, it must offer a rationale stronger than an appearance of balance.

Does calling Russia a US geopolitical enemy require Washington to support Ukraine’s attacks on Russian resources, or can restraint still fit that strategy?

What strategic reason could justify restricting Ukraine’s attacks while still treating Russia as a US adversary?

text:
One sentence from Benjamin Netanyahu this week should have made every ear perk up: “We have two years left of my great friend Donald Trump’s presidency, two years to finish the job.” In that sentence, for the first time in 12 races for prime minister, is Netanyahu marking an end date?

Since 2015 the Likud campaign has toyed with such a declaration, tested it in polls and always backed off at the last moment. It’s called “iron,” the link between the words “prime minister” and “Benjamin Netanyahu.” The original argument is that many swing voters will find it easier to support him for final arrangements for one last job (toppling the regime in Iran, peace with Saudi Arabia and Lebanon) if they know it ends afterward. But in most polls the result is that it deters more voters than it attracts. If it turns out, by mistake, that Netanyahu is a mortal of flesh and blood, and not someone with the prime minister’s office registered in his name in the land registry, then why not vote for someone else?

This time it may be different. First, because Netanyahu, who turned 77 this week, is no longer a kid. Second, because the next American president will in any case be much tougher than the current one. Some people are ready to swear they heard from the prime minister over the past year that he intends to step down around 2028 or 2029, around the end of the 47th president’s term. As is well known, the election for president of the state will be held here in a year and a half, ostensibly a perfect clearing of the desk: closing the open ends in the Middle East, a state role for seven years and an end to the criminal proceedings. It’s all perfect, except that last time he wasn’t interested. His answer to a similar proposal in the previous round, in 2021, was cutting: “If it’s going to be a prison, I’d rather have the original.”

This election offers the oldest gallery to face voters in many years. Netanyahu is in his eighth decade; Avigdor Liberman, the Yisrael Beytenu leader, and Aryeh Deri, the Shas leader, are approaching 70; and former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot and Democrats leader Yair Golan are in their mid-60s. No wonder Naftali Bennett, soon to be 55, boasts of his connection with first-time voters. As in the old joke: young at heart seeks young for her age. For Liberman this may be his last Knesset if he realizes his dream of heading the government. Who knows how long Deri will have the strength, and how many tries Eisenkot and Golan will get.

Personally, I think this is Netanyahu’s last term. And trust me, because that’s exactly what I thought during his past three terms.
